Issues.Title: fix(forms): reject unsupported updateOn in SignalFormControl
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

This was caught while reviewing #70735. This is mostely to warn users that might be suprised by the (lack of) behavior.

## What is the current behavior?

`SignalFormControl` does not support pending or uncommitted values because signal forms are model-driven and react immediately on change. When placed in a `FormGroup` or `FormArray` configured with `updateOn: 'blur'` or `updateOn: 'submit'`, or when initialized with `updateOn` options, `SignalFormControl` would inherit or receive the unsupported option, causing split-brain states or broken submit syncing.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

This commit adds a dev-mode check in `SignalFormControl` to throw an error when:
1. An unsupported `updateOn` option is passed directly in options to the `SignalFormControl` constructor.
2. A non-default `updateOn` option is inherited from a parent `FormGroup` or `FormArray` via `setParent()`.

Additionally, `SignalFormControl` explicitly overrides `get updateOn()` to return `'change'`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(forms): reject unsupported updateOn in SignalFormControl" (#71652)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): update ambient module specifier check for Oxc 0.155
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes the `main` CI build failure in `//packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor/ng-analyze:test` caused by a semantic conflict between #71606 and #71599:

- #71606 added `resolve_ambient_module_member` in `packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor/ng-analyze/src/query/engine.rs`, comparing `decl.id.value.as_str() != specifier`.
- #71599 upgraded `oxc_*` from `0.144.0` to `0.155.0`, where `StringLiteral::value` changed from `Str<'a>` (`.as_str() -> &str`) to `oxc_str::JSStr<'a>` (`.as_str() -> Option<&str>`).

Updates `resolve_ambient_module_member` to use `crate::analyzer::utils::js_str_to_string_lossy(decl.id.value)` consistently with the other `StringLiteral::value` call sites migrated in #71599.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(compiler-cli): update ambient module specifier check for Oxc 0.155" (#71651)

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): implement uninvoked extended diagnostics in preprocessor
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

In NGP (`packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor`), extended template diagnostics run without an in-process `ts.TypeChecker` (designed to support out-of-process TypeScript 7 / `tsgo`). Consequently, the four type-dependent "uninvoked" extended diagnostics were unimplemented (or limited to AST-only arrow/function literals in `NG8111`):

- `interpolatedSignalNotInvoked` (`NG8109`)
- `uninvokedFunctionInEventBinding` (`NG8111`, property/method reads)
- `uninvokedTrackFunction` (`NG8115`)
- `uninvokedFunctionInTextInterpolation` (`NG8117`)

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

Implements all four uninvoked extended diagnostics in the NGP preprocessor via **`.ngtypecheck.ts` type-level probes + diagnostic remapping**:

1. **Private `@angular/core` type-checking helpers (`packages/core/src/type_checking.ts`):**
   - Exposes `@codeGenApi` helpers `ɵassertNotSignal`, `ɵassertNotCallable`, and `ɵassertNotTrackCallable` alongside `ɵassertType` (using `Signal<unknown>` directly and non-distributive conditional types so `any`, `never`, `unknown`, and nullable unions do not produce false positives, with zero per-file declaration boilerplate in `.ngtypecheck.ts` and zero runtime bundle impact).
2. **Candidate collection (`ExtendedTemplateCheckerImpl`):**
   - Extended checks register `TcbExtendedCheckCandidate` entries (`notSignal`, `notCallable`, `notTrackCallable`) with their configured category, pre-formatted `NG8xxx` message, template span, and optional `skipIfTriggered` superseding link (for `NG8109`'s signal/function instance property fallback such as `mySignal.name` / `mySignal.set`).
3. **TCB probe injection & metadata footer (`tcb_ls_util.ts` / `tcb.ts`):**
   - Resolves candidate expressions inside `_tcbN` via trailing span comments (preserving narrowing inside `if`/`switch` and guarding ternary conditional branches).
   - Injects `i1.ɵassertNotSignal(id, expr)`, `i1.ɵassertNotCallable(id, expr)`, and `i1.ɵassertNotTrackCallable(id, expr)` calls using the `@angular/core` namespace import.
   - Emits a `/*ngp-tcb-extended-checks:[...]*/` metadata footer in `.ngtypecheck.ts` so external diagnostic consumers remain completely stateless and require no `ts.TypeChecker` API calls.
4. **Diagnostic remapping & LS filtering (`diagnostic_mapping.ts`, `references_and_rename*.ts`, `ngp_test_driver.ts`):**
   - Remaps `TS2345` errors raised on probe arguments to their Angular extended diagnostic (`code`, `Warning`/`Error` severity, `message`, and exact template span, including external-template `relatedInformation`).
   - Suppresses secondary TypeScript diagnostics (e.g. `TS2339`) inside copied probe expressions so errors on the underlying TCB expression are never duplicated.
   - Filters synthetic probe occurrences out of Language Service Find References and Rename results.
5. **Known limitation:** Distinguishing a 0-arg class method on a `@for` loop variable (`track item.getId`) from a 0-arg callable property (`track field`, e.g. Signal Forms `Field<T>`) cannot be expressed purely at the TypeScript type level (`ts.SymbolFlags.Method` vs `ts.SymbolFlags.Property` have identical structural types `() => K`). Component methods (`track getId`) are flagged via `notCallable`, while other expressions use `notTrackCallable` (flagging `>= 1` required-arg functions while avoiding false positives on 0-arg callable properties).

Removes 75 passing extended diagnostic test cases from `ngp_known_failures.ts` (`NGP_REQUIRES_TYPE_CHECKER`) and adds end-to-end Language Service tests against TypeScript 7 (`tsgo`).

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): make tsconfig optional for the preprocessor analyzer
Issues.Body:
Integrations such as bundlers and the Angular CLI may have no tsconfig at all, or already own
the parsed configuration. The analyzer can now be constructed from options alone.

`AnalyzerOptions.tsconfigPath` is now optional, and three options replace what could
previously only come from the tsconfig:

- `entryPoints`: the roots of the program closure. When set, they replace the tsconfig's root
  files, and the roots are no longer re-read from the tsconfig after file updates (the same
  holds after `setEntryPoints`). Bundlers pass their own entry files; the analyzer follows
  imports from there. The `.d.ts` files a tsconfig lists are still searched for ambient
  modules either way.
- `r3SymbolsFile`: the `r3_symbols.ts` file used when compiling `@angular/core` itself, which
  was only found by scanning the root files for that name. The scan remains the fallback.
- `implicitStandalone`: whether declarations without an explicit `standalone` flag are
  standalone, which was only derived from `angularCompilerOptions._angularCoreVersion`. The
  tsconfig value remains the fallback, and the default is `true`.

`setEntryPoints` is now exposed on every backend (N-API, WASM and the sidecar) and on
`IAnalyzer`, so integrations that discover entry files incrementally can replace the roots
after construction. Like `updateFileContent`, it returns every path whose cached analysis is
now stale.

`createAnalyzer` and `createAnalyzerWithInfo` also accept a single options object in which
`tsconfigPath` is optional, alongside the existing tsconfig-path form, which is unchanged.

Without a tsconfig, every unset option takes its documented default (matching the defaults of
an empty tsconfig), path-valued options must be absolute since there is no directory to
resolve them against, and the module resolver runs without tsconfig `paths` mappings.
Behavior is unchanged when a tsconfig is given and the new options are unset.

Issues.Title: test(forms): measure the AbstractControl cost in signal forms bundles
Issues.Body:
[Issue #71621](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71621) | [Triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-abstract-control-bundle/packages/forms/signals/triage/abstract-control-bundle.md) | [Model-only app](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-abstract-control-bundle/packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals_model/main.ts) | [`[formField]` app](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-abstract-control-bundle/packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals_field/main.ts)

## Why the change

This adds two measurement apps showing that one `instanceof AbstractControl` check costs 10.7% of a minimal signal forms app's gzipped bundle, so that we can agree on the production behavior before I write the fix.

## Special things to note

- This PR is triage only: it changes no library code. Instead of failing specs, it adds two production build targets that measure bundle size. They build without errors.
- The sizes come from the default production build, with mangling, at `3e173fc844`. The list of names that ship comes from an earlier unmangled build, because mangled names can't be read.
- The recommended fix changes production behavior: error `NG1907` would only throw in development. I'd like a decision on that first.

## Change outline

### What this PR adds

```text
packages/core/test/bundling/
├── forms_signals_model/   # form() + required(), no directives
└── forms_signals_field/   # the same form bound with [formField]
packages/forms/signals/triage/abstract-control-bundle.md   # sizes, retained names, fix options
```

### Why reactive forms ship

```text
form()
  new FieldNodeContext(...)
    valueOf = (p) => {                              # instance field, so every form() keeps it
      if (result instanceof AbstractControl) throw NG1907
    }
      AbstractControl                               # from @angular/forms, otherwise unused
        hasValidator(Validators.required) → Validators and its validator functions
        ControlEvent, ValueChangeEvent, StatusChangeEvent, ...
        async validator helpers → RxJS forkJoin, from, schedulers
```

Gzipped `main.js` today:

```text
model only      44,490 B
[formField]     56,835 B
```

With the recommended fix:

```text
model only      39,742 B   (-4,748 B, -10.7%)
[formField]     54,939 B   (-1,896 B, -3.3%)
```

### Recommended fix: run the check in dev mode only

```diff
 // packages/forms/signals/src/field/context.ts, class FieldNodeContext
   readonly valueOf = <TValue>(p: SchemaPath<TValue, SchemaPathRules>) => {
     const result = this.resolve(p)().value();

-    if (result instanceof AbstractControl) {
+    if (ngDevMode && result instanceof AbstractControl) {
       throw new RuntimeError(
         RuntimeErrorCode.ABSTRACT_CONTROL_IN_FORM,
         ngDevMode &&
           `Tried to read an 'AbstractControl' value from a 'form()'. Did you mean to use 'compatForm()' instead?`,
       );
     }
     return result;
   };
```

- **Measured.** The "with the recommended fix" sizes above are this exact change, applied temporarily and then reverted.
- **Development is unchanged.** The error still throws in development. Its message is already dev-only today.
- **Precedent.** `@angular/forms` and signal forms already have dev-only errors, such as the check in `toObservable()` in `validators.ts`.
- **No test changes.** No spec covers `NG1907`, and tests run in dev mode.

### Alternatives

| Option | Change | Tradeoff |
|--------|--------|----------|
| B: a brand check exported privately from `@angular/forms` | `ɵisAbstractControl(value)` reads a symbol getter on `AbstractControl.prototype` | Keeps the production error. Adds a private cross-package export and an API golden update. Not measured |
| C: drop the check | Remove the `if` | Smallest change, but it loses the diagnostic in development too |

### Decisions for maintainers

1. **Production behavior.** Is it acceptable for `NG1907` to throw only in development? In production, a rule that calls `valueOf()` on a `FormControl` in a `form()` model would get the control back.
2. **If not, option B.** Is a private `ɵisAbstractControl()` export from `@angular/forms` acceptable?
3. **Regression guard.** Should these apps become symbol golden tests, like `forms_reactive`? That pattern builds with `NG_BUILD_MANGLE=0` and adds a `js_expected_symbol_test`. Or should the apps be dropped once the fix lands?

Issues.Title: test(forms): reproduce signal form fields outliving the form's injector
Issues.Body:
[Issue #71622](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71622) | [Triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-host-teardown/packages/forms/signals/triage/host-teardown.md) | [Failing specs](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-host-teardown/packages/forms/signals/test/node/form_host_teardown.spec.ts)

## Why the change

This adds failing specs showing that destroying a signal form's host leaves its fields alive, so that we can agree on the teardown contract before I write the fix.

## Special things to note

- This PR is triage only: it changes no library code. Five of its six specs fail on purpose. A fix should make them pass, and they then stay as regression tests.
- The recommended fix is about 15 lines. It also makes "a form's fields end with the form's injector" a contract, and I'd like a decision on that first (see the end).
- The recommended fix changes `FieldNodeStructure.destroy()`, which the injector-per-field triage (#71623) also changes. Either can land first.

## Change outline

### What this PR adds

```text
packages/forms/signals/
├── test/node/form_host_teardown.spec.ts   # 5 failing specs, 1 passing control spec
└── triage/host-teardown.md           # spec output, root cause with links, fix options
```

### Who destroys a field today

A field creates its own `R3Injector` on first use, as a child of the form's injector. An `R3Injector` doesn't register with its parent, so only the cleanup sweep ever destroys a field, and the sweep only handles fields that were removed from the model.

```text
form(model, schema, {injector})                     # injector: a component's or an environment injector
  FormFieldManager(injector)
    effect(sweep, {injector})                       # dies with the host
      destroys structures no longer reachable from the root
  root FieldNodeStructure                           # never in `structures`, so never swept
    get injector() → Injector.create({parent: injector})
  child FieldNodeStructure → fieldManager.structures.add(this)
    get injector() → Injector.create({parent: injector})
```

When the host is destroyed, today:

```text
host.destroy()
  sweep effect: destroyed
  root field injector: alive
  child field injectors: alive
    validateAsync() resources: in-flight load not aborted
    DestroyRef callbacks from managed metadata keys: not called
```

After the recommended fix:

```text
host.destroy()
  sweep effect: destroyed
  root field injector: destroyed
  child field injectors: destroyed
    validateAsync() resources: in-flight load aborted
    DestroyRef callbacks from managed metadata keys: called once
```

### Recommended fix: the field manager destroys every field with the host

`FormFieldManager` registers one `DestroyRef` hook per form. The root joins `structures`, so the hook reaches it.

```diff
 // packages/forms/signals/src/field/manager.ts
   createFieldManagementEffect(root: FieldNodeStructure): void {
     effect(
       () => {
         const liveStructures = new Set<FieldNodeStructure>();
         this.markStructuresLive(root, liveStructures);

         // Destroy all nodes that are no longer live.
         for (const structure of this.structures) {
           if (!liveStructures.has(structure)) {
             this.structures.delete(structure);
             untracked(() => structure.destroy());
           }
         }
       },
       {injector: this.injector},
     );
+
+    this.injector.get(DestroyRef).onDestroy(() => {
+      for (const structure of this.structures) {
+        structure.destroy();
+      }
+      this.structures.clear();
+    });
   }
```

```diff
 // packages/forms/signals/src/field/structure.ts
 export class RootFieldNodeStructure extends FieldNodeStructure {
   constructor(/* ... */) {
     super(logic, node, createChildNode);
     this.childrenMap = this.createChildrenMap();
+    // The sweep always marks the root live, so only the host's teardown destroys it.
+    this.fieldManager.structures.add(this);
   }
 }

 // class FieldNodeStructure
   destroy(): void {
-    this.injector.destroy();
+    this._injector?.destroy();
   }
```

- **No double destroy.** The sweep removes a structure from `structures` before destroying it, so the hook destroys only what's left. `R3Injector.destroy()` throws if it runs twice.
- **Both host kinds work.** A component's injector returns its view's `DestroyRef`, and an environment injector returns itself.
- **`compatForm()`.** `CompatStructure` doesn't join `structures` either. It needs the same `structures.add(this)` after it assigns `fieldManager`.
- **Cost.** One hook per form.

### Alternatives

| Option | Change | Tradeoff |
|--------|--------|----------|
| 1B: each field injector registers with the host | In the `injector` getter, register `injector.destroy()` on the parent's `DestroyRef` and unregister when the field is swept | No registry, and the root and compat fields are covered for free. But it adds one host hook per field, and unregistering during host teardown needs care |
| 1C: replace per-field `R3Injector`s with a lightweight field scope | A small `Injector` that serves its own `DestroyRef` and delegates everything else to the form's injector. Child scopes register on their parent scope | Also removes the per-field injector cost from #71623. It's a larger change: `INJECTOR`, `destroyed`, and `EnvironmentInjector` lookups need handling |

The triage note has the full code for each option.

### Decisions for maintainers

1. **Contract.** Should destroying a form's injector destroy all of its fields? Nothing documents this today. The `injector` option's docs only mention dependency injection. The guide says cleanup is tied to "the field's lifecycle" but never says when that ends.
2. **Use after teardown.** After the fix, a field that's first read after its host is destroyed gets an injector whose parent is destroyed, and nothing ever sweeps it. Should that throw a clear error, return an inert field, or stay undefined?
3. **Mechanism.** 1A keeps per-field `R3Injector`s. If you'd rather replace them (1C), I'd fold this fix into that change instead.

Issues.Title: test(forms): reproduce unneeded field injectors in signal forms
Issues.Body:
[Issue #71623](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71623) | [Triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-injector-allocation/packages/forms/signals/triage/injector-allocation.md) | [Failing specs](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-injector-allocation/packages/forms/signals/test/node/field_injector_allocation.spec.ts)

## Why the change

This adds failing specs showing that signal form fields create injectors that nothing uses, so that we can agree on the scope of the fix before I write it.

## Special things to note

- This PR is triage only: it changes no library code. Both specs fail on purpose. A fix should make them pass, and they then stay as regression tests.
- The specs count calls to `Injector.create`, which ties them to the implementation. I couldn't find a public signal for "this field has an injector".
- The recommended fix changes `FieldNodeStructure.destroy()`, which the host teardown triage (#71622) also changes. Either can land first.

## Change outline

### What this PR adds

```text
packages/forms/signals/
├── test/node/field_injector_allocation.spec.ts   # 2 failing specs
└── triage/injector-allocation.md                 # spec output, root cause with links, fix options
```

### Where the injector comes from

```text
new FieldNode(...)
  metadataState.runMetadataCreateLifecycle()
    if the field has no metadata keys: return        # no rule, or validate() only
    runInInjectionContext(structure.injector, ...)   # the getter creates an R3Injector here
      for each metadata key
        if key.create: key.create(...)               # only managed keys, such as validateAsync()

cleanup sweep: a field was removed from the model
  structure.destroy()
    this.injector.destroy()                          # the getter creates an injector if there was none
```

`Injector.create` calls for a form over 50 array items, with one rule on each item, today:

```text
no rule            0
validate()         0
required()        50
min()             50
debounce()        50
validateAsync()   50
remove 50 items without a rule: 50
```

After the recommended fix:

```text
no rule            0
validate()         0
required()         0
min()              0
debounce()         0
validateAsync()   50
remove 50 items without a rule: 0
```

### Recommended fix: enter an injection context only for managed keys

```diff
 // packages/forms/signals/src/field/metadata.ts, class FieldMetadataState
   runMetadataCreateLifecycle(): void {
     // ...early return and params-flag handling unchanged...
-      untracked(() =>
-        runInInjectionContext(this.node.structure.injector, () => {
-          for (const key of this.node.logicNode.logic.getMetadataKeys()) {
-            if (key.create) {
-              /* create the managed value */
-            }
-          }
-        }),
-      );
+      untracked(() => {
+        for (const key of logic.getMetadataKeys()) {
+          if (!key.create) {
+            continue;
+          }
+          // Only managed keys need the field's injector, so it's created here and nowhere else.
+          runInInjectionContext(this.node.structure.injector, () => {
+            /* create the managed value, unchanged */
+          });
+        }
+      });
   }
```

```diff
 // packages/forms/signals/src/field/structure.ts, class FieldNodeStructure
   destroy(): void {
-    this.injector.destroy();
+    this._injector?.destroy();
   }
```

- **Same contract.** A managed key's `create` still runs in the field's injection context, which is all the guide promises. Plain keys only build a `computed()`.
- **No other readers.** Nothing else reads a field's injector. `compatForm()` children read the root's injector, and that read stays lazy.
- **Cost.** A field with several managed keys enters the injection context once per key instead of once.

### Alternatives

| Option | Change | Tradeoff |
|--------|--------|----------|
| B: cache "has managed keys" on the logic node | Return early from `runMetadataCreateLifecycle()` when no key has `create` | Also skips the key loop. But `getMetadata()` adds keys lazily, so a cached flag could go stale |
| C: a lightweight field scope instead of an `R3Injector` | Option C in the host teardown triage | Makes managed keys cheaper too. Much larger change |

### Decisions for maintainers

1. **Injection context scope.** Do you want every field with metadata to keep an injection context, for example for planned features? Option A narrows it to managed keys, which matches what the guide documents.
2. **How much this matters.** One injector costs about 1.1 to 1.5 µs to create in Node, and I didn't measure memory. Is that worth a fix now, or should it wait for the lightweight scope?
3. **Test style.** Is counting `Injector.create` calls acceptable in a regression test, or would you prefer another check?

Issues.Title: test(forms): add repro specs for compat parse errors
Issues.Body:
[Issue #71633](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71633) | [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/9a747b865e1f4725fde103a947f5308ce8d1b365/packages/forms/signals/triage/compat-parse-errors.md) | [Repro specs](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/9a747b865e1f4725fde103a947f5308ce8d1b365/packages/forms/signals/test/web/compat_parse_errors.spec.ts)

## Why the change

A `compatForm()` field drops the parse errors its controls report, so bad input leaves the field valid and `submit()` runs with the last good value; this draft adds a failing repro spec and asks you to settle how compat validity should work before I write the fix.

## Special things to note

- This is a triage draft with no fix. The repro spec fails on purpose, so CI is red.
- The fix makes a compat field report `invalid` while its `FormControl` still reports valid. That
  split is the main decision below.
- A related bug, `FormControl` errors missing from `errorSummary()`, has its own triage PR:
  #71630. Both fixes change `CompatValidationState`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Change outline

What the branch adds:

```text
packages/forms/signals/
├── test/web/compat_parse_errors.spec.ts   # 1 failing repro, 1 passing control spec
└── triage/compat-parse-errors.md          # observed output, root cause, history
```

Where a parse error goes, for `<input type="number" [formField]="f.age">` with `5e` typed:

```diff
 FormField.parseErrors()              → [{kind: 'parse'}]
 CompatValidationState
-  parseErrors                        → []  (hardcoded)
-  errors, valid, invalid, syncValid  → the FormControl only
+  parseErrors                        → the parse errors of every binding
+  errors                             → parse errors, then the FormControl's errors
+  valid, syncValid                   → the FormControl's value, and no parse errors
+  invalid                            → the FormControl's value, or any parse error
 FormField.errors()                   (filters the field's errors())
-  → []
+  → [{kind: 'parse'}]
 submit(f, action)
-  runs the action; the model still holds 5
+  doesn't run the action
```

### Recommended fix: merge binding parse errors in the compat layer

Do what `FieldValidationState` does (`compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts`):

```diff
-  readonly errors: Signal<CompatValidationError[]>;
+  readonly errors: Signal<ValidationError.WithFieldTree[]>;

-  readonly parseErrors: Signal<ValidationError.WithFormField[]> = computed(() => []);
+  readonly parseErrors: Signal<ValidationError.WithFormField[]> = computed(
+    () => this.node.formFieldBindings().flatMap((binding) => binding.parseErrors()),
+    {equal: shallowArrayEquals},
+  );

   constructor(private readonly node: CompatFieldNode, options: CompatFieldNodeOptions) {
-    this.syncValid = getControlStatusSignal(options, (c) => c.status === 'VALID');
-    this.errors = getControlStatusSignal(options, extractNestedReactiveErrors);
-    this.valid = getControlStatusSignal(options, (c) => c.valid);
-    this.invalid = getControlStatusSignal(options, (c) => c.invalid);
+    const controlSyncValid = getControlStatusSignal(options, (c) => c.status === 'VALID');
+    const controlErrors = getControlStatusSignal(options, extractNestedReactiveErrors);
+    const controlValid = getControlStatusSignal(options, (c) => c.valid);
+    const controlInvalid = getControlStatusSignal(options, (c) => c.invalid);
+    const hasParseErrors = computed(() => this.parseErrors().length > 0);
+
+    this.errors = computed(() => [...this.parseErrors(), ...controlErrors()], {
+      equal: shallowArrayEquals,
+    });
+    this.syncValid = computed(() => controlSyncValid() && !hasParseErrors());
+    this.valid = computed(() => controlValid() && !hasParseErrors());
+    this.invalid = computed(() => controlInvalid() || hasParseErrors());
     this.pending = getControlStatusSignal(options, (c) => c.pending);
   }
```

`status` already derives from `errors()` and `pending()`. That covers both submit paths: a compat
root reads its own `invalid` and `valid`, and a plain root reads each compat child's `status()`.

### Alternatives considered

- **Write parse errors into the `FormControl` with `setErrors()`.** The next
  `updateValueAndValidity()` wipes them, and it fights reactive forms' ownership of the control.
  Not recommended.
- **Only document the limitation.** This is the cheapest option, but it leaves a silent submit with
  the wrong value.

### Design decisions

1. **Signal-layer validity and `FormControl` validity disagree.** After the fix,
   `f.age().invalid()` is `true` while `FormControl.valid` and its parent `FormGroup.valid` stay
   `true`. Code that gates on the reactive status disagrees with `submit()`. The migration guide says
   "Reactive state is proxied automatically" (`migration.md:46`), so the guide needs a sentence on
   this. Today compat is worse than both APIs it bridges: reactive forms' `NumberValueAccessor`
   writes `null` for bad input, so `Validators.required` catches it, and plain signal forms block the
   submit.
2. **Error types in `errors()`.** The guide says `errors()` returns `CompatValidationError`
   (`migration.md:48`). After the fix, parse errors appear too, and they have no `control` or
   `context`. The public type doesn't change, because `compatForm()` returns a plain `FieldTree`.
   The `errorMessage()` helper the guide added on `main` already handles this: it checks
   `instanceof CompatValidationError` and falls back to `error.message ?? error.kind`.
3. **Order.** Parse errors come first, as in `FieldValidationState`.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Is it acceptable for a compat field to report `invalid` while its `FormControl` reports valid,
   with a sentence in the migration guide?
2. Should parse errors come before the `FormControl`'s errors in `errors()`, as they do on plain
   fields?

---

Issues.Title: test(forms): add repro specs for per-control parse errors
Issues.Body:
[Issue #71632](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71632) | [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/7e43a71da8e7763a078ac5c4dbbe0d847ef52efa/packages/forms/signals/triage/errors-per-control.md) | [Repro specs](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/7e43a71da8e7763a078ac5c4dbbe0d847ef52efa/packages/forms/signals/test/web/form_field_errors_per_binding.spec.ts)

## Why the change

When one field has several controls, CVA and native hosts receive every control's parse errors instead of only their own, a regression from the refactor that moved control logic into `FormField`; this draft adds failing repro specs and asks you to confirm the intended behavior before I write the fix.

## Special things to note

- This is a triage draft with no fix. The 2 repro specs fail on purpose, so CI is red.
- The intent is already on record: `ebae211add` filtered `errors` per control for every host, and
  `a67e00741c` kept the filter only for custom controls.
- `invalid` stays field-level. Every control still receives `invalid: true`.

## Change outline

What the branch adds:

```text
packages/forms/signals/
├── test/web/form_field_errors_per_binding.spec.ts   # 2 failing repros
└── triage/errors-per-control.md                     # observed output, history, NgControl path
```

How each host reads `errors` today:

```text
custom host   control_custom.ts   parent.errors()                            filtered per binding
CVA host      control_cva.ts      readFieldStateBindingValue(fieldState)     unfiltered
native host   control_native.ts   readFieldStateBindingValue(state)          unfiltered
NgControl     InteropNgControl    field().errors()                           unfiltered
```

### Recommended fix: one code path for every host

`src/directive/bindings.ts`:

```diff
 export function readFieldStateBindingValue(
-  fieldState: ReadonlyFieldState<unknown>,
+  parent: FormField<unknown>,
   key: ControlBindingKey,
 ): unknown {
+  // `FormField.errors` drops parse errors that belong to other bindings of the same field.
+  if (key === FIELD_STATE_KEY_TO_CONTROL_BINDING.errors) {
+    return parent.errors();
+  }
   const property = CONTROL_BINDING_TO_FIELD_STATE_KEY[key];
-  return fieldState[property]?.();
+  return parent.state()[property]?.();
 }
```

`src/directive/control_custom.ts` drops its special case:

```diff
     for (const name of CONTROL_BINDING_NAMES) {
-      let value: unknown;
-      if (name === 'errors') {
-        value = parent.errors();
-      } else {
-        value = readFieldStateBindingValue(state, name);
-      }
+      const value = readFieldStateBindingValue(parent, name);
```

`src/directive/control_cva.ts` and `src/directive/control_native.ts`:

```diff
-      const value = readFieldStateBindingValue(fieldState, name);
+      const value = readFieldStateBindingValue(parent, name);
```

### Optional, same intent: `NgControl.errors`

`FormField` creates one `InteropNgControl` per binding, but builds it from the field state only, so
`inject(NgControl).errors` has the same leak:

```diff
 // src/directive/form_field.ts
   get interopNgControl(): InteropNgControl {
-    return (this._interopNgControl ??= new InteropNgControl(this.state));
+    return (this._interopNgControl ??= new InteropNgControl(this.state, this.errors));
   }

 // src/controls/interop_ng_control.ts
-  constructor(protected field: () => ReadonlyFieldState<unknown>) {}
+  constructor(
+    protected field: () => ReadonlyFieldState<unknown>,
+    private readonly bindingErrors: () => readonly ValidationError[],
+  ) {}

   get errors(): ValidationErrors | null {
-    return signalErrorsToValidationErrors(this.field().errors());
+    return signalErrorsToValidationErrors(this.bindingErrors());
   }
```

### Alternative considered

Copy the special case from `control_custom.ts` into `control_cva.ts` and `control_native.ts`. That's
the smallest diff, but keeping three copies is how the behavior drifted.

### Design decisions

1. **Per-control `errors` for every host.** Recommended, because it restores the documented intent.
   `ebae211add` says: "we only want to report parse errors that are relevant for this particular UI
   control." `22afbb2f36` says a native parse error "is added for the control that received the
   un-parsable value."
2. **`invalid` stays field-level.** It was never filtered, even in `ebae211add`. A control can
   receive `invalid: true` with an empty `errors`, which is what custom controls get today.
3. **Scope.** Include `NgControl.errors` in the same fix, or leave it for a follow-up. CVA
   components written for reactive forms often read `NgControl.errors` to show their own error
   state.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Can you confirm that every host should receive only its own binding's parse errors, as custom
   controls do today?
2. Should `NgControl.errors` be filtered in the same PR?
3. Is it intended that a control receives `invalid: true` with no `errors` when another control on
   the same field has the parse error?

---

Issues.Title: test(forms): add repro specs for compat errorSummary
Issues.Body:
[Issue #71634](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71634) | [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/df91c393eb29637719c4f8bcd5608fbaf23d6092/packages/forms/signals/triage/compat-error-summary.md) | [Repro specs](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/df91c393eb29637719c4f8bcd5608fbaf23d6092/packages/forms/signals/test/node/compat/compat_error_summary.spec.ts)

## Why the change

A `compatForm()` field's `errorSummary` is always empty and its errors carry no `fieldTree`, so the root's `errorSummary()` hides every `FormControl` error while the form is invalid; this draft adds failing repro specs and asks you to confirm the fix shape before I write it.

## Special things to note

- This is a triage draft with no fix. The 2 repro specs fail on purpose, so CI is red.
- The summary fix depends on `fieldTree`: the root summary sorts errors by DOM position through
  `error.fieldTree()`, so returning compat errors without it would throw.
- #71628 also changes `CompatValidationState`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Change outline

What the branch adds:

```text
packages/forms/signals/
├── test/node/compat/compat_error_summary.spec.ts   # 2 failing repros, 1 passing control spec
└── triage/compat-error-summary.md                  # observed output, root cause, sort hazard
```

State of `f = compatForm(signal({name: new FormControl('', Validators.required)}))`:

```diff
 f.name().errors()
-  → [{kind: 'required', fieldTree: undefined}]
+  → [{kind: 'required', fieldTree: f.name}]
 f.name().errorSummary()                 shared EMPTY_ARRAY_SIGNAL today
-  → []
+  → [{kind: 'required', fieldTree: f.name}]
 f().errorSummary()                      the root's errors, then each child's summary
-  → []
+  → [{kind: 'required', fieldTree: f.name}]
 f().invalid()
   → true
```

Why `fieldTree` has to come first:

```text
f().errorSummary()
  reduceChildren(errors, child.errorSummary())
  errors.sort(compareErrorPosition)           client only
    getFirstBoundElement(error)
      error.formField?.element                undefined for FormControl errors
      error.fieldTree().formFieldBindings()   TypeError when fieldTree is undefined
```

### Recommended fix

Point each `FormControl` error at its compat field with `addDefaultField()`, the helper plain
validation rules already use, and make the summary the field's own errors
(`compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts`):

```diff
-    this.errors = getControlStatusSignal(options, extractNestedReactiveErrors);
+    // Point each `FormControl` error at this field, like plain validation rules do.
+    this.errors = getControlStatusSignal(options, (c) =>
+      addDefaultField(extractNestedReactiveErrors(c), this.node.fieldTree),
+    );

-  errorSummary: Signal<ValidationError.WithFieldTree[]> = EMPTY_ARRAY_SIGNAL;
+  // A compat field has no children, so its summary is its own errors.
+  get errorSummary(): Signal<ValidationError.WithFieldTree[]> {
+    return this.errors;
+  }
```

`extractNestedReactiveErrors()` creates new error objects on every status change, so setting
`fieldTree` on them doesn't touch shared state.

### Alternative considered

Add a `fieldTree` parameter to `CompatValidationError`'s constructor. That's a public API change,
and `extractNestedReactiveErrors()` would need the field passed down. Not recommended.

### Design decisions

1. **What a compat field's summary holds.** Its own errors, including the nested errors of a
   `FormGroup` or `FormArray` value. All of them point at the compat field, because nested controls
   have no `FieldTree` of their own.
2. **Where `fieldTree` is set.** In `CompatValidationState`, so the public `CompatValidationError`
   class doesn't change.
3. **Sort order.** A compat field that's bound with `[formControl]` instead of `[formField]` has no
   bound element, so its errors sort to the end of the root summary.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Is a compat field's own `errors()` the right summary, with nested `FormControl` errors pointing
   at the compat field?
2. Is `addDefaultField()` in `CompatValidationState` the right place to set `fieldTree`, rather than
   the `CompatValidationError` constructor?
3. Is it acceptable that errors of compat fields without a `[formField]` binding sort last?

---

Issues.Title: test(forms): reproduce the cleanup sweep materializing all fields
Issues.Body:
[Issue #70627](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/70627) | [Triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-sweep-materialization/packages/forms/signals/triage/sweep-materialization.md) | [Failing specs](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-sweep-materialization/packages/forms/signals/test/node/field_tree_cleanup_laziness.spec.ts) | [Earlier fix #70633 (closed)](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/70633)

## Why the change

This adds failing specs showing that the field cleanup sweep creates every field of a signal form on its first run, so that we can agree on the fix before I write it.

## Special things to note

- This PR is triage only: it changes no library code. Three of its four specs fail on purpose. A fix should make them pass, and they then stay as regression tests.
- An earlier fix, #70633, made the same one-line change as option A below. Its author closed it a week after opening it, with no review and no tests, and it's now locked. I applied option A temporarily: all four specs pass, and so do the full node and Chromium suites.
- Laziness touches open work: #71150 changes how `markAsTouched()` walks children, and #71623 shows that every created field with a rule gets its own injector.

## Change outline

### What this PR adds

```text
packages/forms/signals/
├── test/node/field_tree_cleanup_laziness.spec.ts   # 3 failing specs, 1 passing control spec
└── triage/sweep-materialization.md                # spec output, root cause with links, fix options
```

### How the sweep creates every field

```text
form(signal({rows: [100 rows]}))     # 0 child fields: nothing has read them
  first effect flush
    field-management effect
      markStructuresLive(root)
        root.structure.children()
          ensureChildrenMap()
            computeChildrenMap(value, prev, forceMaterialize = true)   # creates rows
        for each child: markStructuresLive(child)                      # recurses into every row and leaf
```

Child fields for a form over 100 rows without rules, today:

```text
after form()          0
after first tick    301   (rows, 100 rows, 200 leaves)
```

After the recommended fix:

```text
after form()          0
after first tick      0   (a row is created when something reads it, such as f.rows[3]())
```

### Recommended fix: the sweep walks only fields that already exist

```diff
 // packages/forms/signals/src/field/manager.ts
   private markStructuresLive(
     structure: FieldNodeStructure,
     liveStructures: Set<FieldNodeStructure>,
   ): void {
     liveStructures.add(structure);
-    for (const child of structure.children()) {
+    for (const child of structure.materializedChildren()) {
       this.markStructuresLive(child.structure, liveStructures);
     }
   }
```

A leaf also skips a redundant `childrenMap` write on every `children()` call:

```diff
 // packages/forms/signals/src/field/structure.ts, class FieldNodeStructure
   private ensureChildrenMap() {
     // If we're already materialized, there's nothing to do.
-    if (this._areChildrenMaterialized()) {
+    if (this._areChildrenMaterialized() || !isObject(untracked(this.value))) {
       return;
     }
```

- **Cleanup still works.** A field that was never created has nothing to destroy. `materializedChildren()` still reads `childrenMap()`, so the sweep reruns when the model changes shape. The control spec removes a row that was read and checks that it's destroyed.
- **Only the sweep becomes lazy.** `markAsTouched()`, `reloadValidation()`, focus, and WebMCP schema inference still call `children()`.

### Alternatives

| Option | Change | Tradeoff |
|--------|--------|----------|
| B: destroy children where they're removed | `computeChildrenMap()` queues dropped fields, and the effect drains the queue | Avoids walking the materialized tree on each change. But the queue needs its own reactive trigger, and tracked array items can move instead of being removed |
| C: make `children()` stop materializing | Change `children()` itself | Changes every caller. For example, a field read for the first time after `submit()` would start untouched. Not recommended |

### Decisions for maintainers

1. **Scope of laziness.** Is laziness a contract only for the cleanup sweep, or for every internal walker? If it's every walker, `markAsTouched()` and `reloadValidation()` need the same treatment, and #71150 already starts on `markAsTouched()`.
2. **Leaf guard.** Include it in the same fix, or leave it out? It only saves a write that doesn't notify anyone.
3. **Test style.** The specs read internals: `_areChildrenMaterialized()`, `fieldManager.structures`, and a spy on `childrenMap.update`. Is that acceptable, or would you prefer another check?

---

Issues.Title: test(forms): reproduce stale debounced async validation results
Issues.Body:
[Issue #71636](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71636) | [Triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/forms/signals/triage/debounce-pending-window.md) | [Forms spec](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/forms/signals/test/node/validate_async_debounce_window.spec.ts) | [Core spec](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/core/test/resource/debounce_status_spec.ts) | [Stuck fix #71414](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71414)

## Why the change

This adds failing specs showing that a debounced async validator keeps its old result instead of reporting `pending` right after a value change, so that we can agree on a fix in `@angular/core` before I write it.

## Special things to note

- This PR is triage only: it changes no library code. Three of its four specs fail on purpose. I applied option A below temporarily: all four pass, and so do the core resource suites (Node, Chromium, Firefox) and the signal forms suites (Node, Chromium).
- #71414 is stuck. The [review on Oct 25](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71414#pullrequestreview-5640773489) requested changes, said that the gap isn't specific to signal forms because `@angular/core` has no snapshot-based chaining primitive, and objected to keeping the previous settled value while debouncing. Its author replied that it "seems to be unfixable without breaking changes or creating a new API". Option A follows the review: it removes the stale `resolved` state in core `debounced()` itself, for every `chain(debounced(...))` user.
- Option A doesn't fix #70884. It makes the #70884 pattern throw as soon as the value changes instead of after effects run (measured). A snapshot-based chaining primitive, as the review suggests, would fix #70884 and works together with option A.

## Change outline

### What this PR adds

```text
packages/core/test/resource/debounce_status_spec.ts                # 2 failing specs: the root cause
packages/forms/signals/
├── test/node/validate_async_debounce_window.spec.ts               # 1 failing spec, 1 passing control spec
└── triage/debounce-pending-window.md                              # spec output, root cause, measurements, fix options
```

### Where the stale state comes from

```text
f().value.set('VALID')                       # the validator settled on 'INVALID' before
  validateAsync params                       → 'VALID'
  debounced(params, 50)
    linkedSignal computation                 # previous state exists, so it's kept: resolved 'INVALID'
    effect (runs later)                      # sets loading and starts the timer
  computed(() => ɵchain(debounced))          → 'INVALID', because chain() only throws while loading
  resource request                           # unchanged, so status stays resolved with the old result
```

State read in the same task as `value.set('VALID')`, today:

```text
debounced status    resolved ('INVALID')
field pending()     false
field invalid()     true, the old result
submit()            the action doesn't run
```

After option A:

```text
debounced status    loading (value 'INVALID')
field pending()     true
field invalid()     false
submit()            the action runs, as it does without debounce
```

### Recommended fix: `debounced()` reports `loading` as soon as its source changes

```diff
 // packages/core/src/resource/debounce.ts, debounced()
+  const equal = options?.equal ?? Object.is;
+
   const state = linkedSignal<...>({
     source: () => { /* unchanged */ },
     computation: (res, previous) => {
-      // If we already have a state from the effect or a previous read, keep it!
-      // The effect is responsible for timing and state transitions.
       if (previous !== undefined) {
-        return previous.value;
+        // The effect owns timing, but a changed source is pending from the moment it changes.
+        const prev = previous.value;
+        if (!res.thrown && prev.status === 'resolved' && !equal(res.value, prev.value)) {
+          return {status: 'loading', value: prev.value};
+        }
+        return prev;
       }
       /* first evaluation unchanged */
     },
   });

   effect(() => {
     /* ...read the source, unchanged... */
     const currentState = untracked(state);
-    const equal = options?.equal ?? Object.is;
-    if (currentState.status === 'reloading' || currentState.status === 'loading') {
+    // Compare with the value being waited on, or else with the settled value.
+    if (active !== undefined) {
       if (equal(value, pendingValue!)) return;
     } else if (currentState.status === 'resolved') {
       if (equal(value, currentState.value!)) return;
     }
```

- **The effect guard has to change.** The state can now be `loading` before any wait has started. With the old guard, a source that changes to `undefined`, which forms uses when validation is skipped, would match `pendingValue` and stay `loading` forever.
- **The fix is in core.** Forms doesn't change. Any app that reads a `chain(debounced(...))` resource right after a write gets `loading` as well.
- **Synchronous waits.** A `wait` function that returns `undefined` shows `loading` until effects flush. Templates don't see it.
- **#70884 throws sooner.** For a snapshot-based factory over `chain(debounced(...))`, a read in the same task as the write throws `LOADING` with option A, and returns the stale value today. Both throw after `TestBed.tick()`. Factories built with `resource()` aren't affected.

### Alternatives

| Option | Change | Tradeoff |
|--------|--------|----------|
| B: `validateAsync()` treats a params mismatch as pending | Throw `ResourceParamsStatus.LOADING` while the debounced value differs from the params | Forms only. Needs a new private export from core. Not measured |
| C: WebMCP waits for the app to be stable before submitting | `await injector.get(ApplicationRef).whenStable()` in `execute` | Mitigation only. It also waits for unrelated work |

### Decisions for maintainers

1. **`debounced()` contract.** Should `status()` turn `loading` at the moment the source changes? The `debounced()` guide says that it "tells you whether a new value is still pending".
2. **Order with #70884.** Should option A land on its own, so that the #70884 pattern fails a little sooner but in the same way, or together with the snapshot-based chaining primitive from the #71414 review?
3. **Synchronous waits.** Is a brief `loading` state acceptable for a `wait` function that returns `undefined`? The alternative is to report `loading` only for a numeric `wait`, which leaves custom async `wait` functions with today's window.

Issues.Title: fix(core): prevent window.opener exposure in sanitized HTML links
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The HTML sanitizer allowlists both `rel` and `target` attributes without filtering `rel` tokens or accounting for custom named `target` browsing contexts. Consequently, untrusted HTML passed through `[innerHTML]` or `DomSanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, ...)` can retain `rel="opener"` (which opts out of modern browsers' implicit `noopener` default on `target="_blank"`) or specify a custom `target` window name (which does not receive implicit `noopener`), exposing `window.opener` to newly opened tabs.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

- Strips the `opener` token (ASCII case-insensitively across ASCII whitespace) from `rel` attributes in `SanitizingHtmlSerializer` (omitting `rel` completely if `opener` was its sole token, and recording `sanitizedSomething = true`).
- Ensures `noopener` is present in `rel` (unless `noopener` or `noreferrer` is already present) on `<a>` and `<area>` elements with custom `target` browsing context names (any non-empty value other than `_blank`, `_self`, `_parent`, or `_top`), while leaving standard `target="_blank"` without `rel="opener"` untouched.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: refactor(forms): correct the InputValidityMonitor doc comment
Issues.Body:
[Service introduced in #67416](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/67416)

## Why the change

The `InputValidityMonitor` doc comment describes a CSS transition and a `transitionstart` listener, but the service has always used `@keyframes` animations and `animationstart`, so this corrects the comment and renames the private `createTransitionStyle()` to match.

## Special things to note

- No behavior change: only the doc comment and one private method name change.

## Change outline

The doc comment in `packages/forms/signals/src/directive/input_validity_monitor.ts`:

```diff
 /**
  * Service that monitors validity state changes on native form elements.
  *
- * It works by dynamically installing a CSS transition on `input, textarea` `:valid`
- * and `:invalid` states, which allows us to intercept a `transitionstart` event
- * whenever the native validity state changes without an `input` event (e.g. clearing a date input).
+ * It works by dynamically installing a CSS animation on the `:valid` and `:invalid` states of
+ * `input` and `textarea` elements. Each state uses a differently named animation, so a validity
+ * change restarts the animation and fires an `animationstart` event, even when no `input` event
+ * fires (e.g. clearing a date input).
  */
```

What the code does, which this PR doesn't change:

```diff
 AnimationInputValidityMonitor.watchValidity(element)
-  createTransitionStyle(rootNode)
+  createAnimationStyle(rootNode)
     @keyframes ng-valid {}
     @keyframes ng-invalid {}
     input:valid, textarea:valid      → animation: ng-valid 0.001s
     input:invalid, textarea:invalid  → animation: ng-invalid 0.001s
   element.addEventListener('animationstart', …)
     animationName is ng-valid or ng-invalid → callback()
```

Issues.Title: test(forms): add missing assertions to two signal forms specs
Issues.Body:
## Why the change

Two signal forms specs set up behavior but never assert it, so they would keep passing if async validation stopped running after a debounce, or if removing an array item stopped aborting its in-flight validation; this adds the missing assertions.

## Special things to note

- Test-only. Both specs pass with the new assertions.
- `debounced()` registers no pending task, so `whenStable()` returns in the middle of the debounce.
  The spec now uses `useAutoTick()` and waits with `timeout(300)`.
- The test component's `form` changes from `protected` to `readonly`, so the spec can read the field.

## Change outline

`test/web/debounce_async_validation_bug.spec.ts` ("should not throw a cycle error when using
debounced in validateAsync factory") had no expectations. It now checks each step:

```text
step                              loads                  hello()
first render + whenStable()       ['world']              pending() false
type "hello!" + whenStable()      ['world']              value() 'hello!', pending() true
timeout(300) + whenStable()       ['world', 'hello!']    pending() false, valid() true
```

Before this change, the spec ended at the second step, before the debounced load started.

`test/web/orphan_repro.spec.ts` ("should handle validateAsync resolving after the field is
orphaned") registered abort listeners but never checked them. It now records each load by its
params and checks the abort state after the second item is removed:

```diff
-                loader: ({abortSignal}) => {
+                loader: ({params, abortSignal}) => {
+                  loads.push({params, abortSignal});
 ...
     // Force CD synchronously to trigger structure removal and orphan the node
     appRef.tick();

+    // Removing 'two' aborts its in-flight load and leaves the load for 'one' running.
+    const aborted = Object.fromEntries(loads.map((l) => [l.params, l.abortSignal.aborted]));
+    expect(aborted).toEqual({one: false, two: true});
```

Issues.Title: Signal forms: right after a value change, a debounced async validator reports the old result instead of `pending`
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms, core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

A field with `validateAsync({debounce})` or `validateHttp({debounce})` doesn't report `pending()` right after its value changes. Until Angular runs effects, the field keeps the async result for the previous value. Code that changes a value and then reads the form's state or calls `submit()` in the same task acts on that old result.

Without `debounce`, the same field reports `pending()` at once.

**Why it matters.**

- WebMCP's tool `execute` sets the value and submits in the same task. By reading the code, an AI agent that corrects an invalid value gets "Form submission failed" with the error for the old value.
- An app that sets a value and submits in one handler, for example from a keyboard shortcut, sees the same failure.
- The [async operations guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/async-operations.md?plain=1#L668) says that "validation always reflects the current value".

The cause is in `debounced()` in `@angular/core`, so any app that reads a `chain(debounced(...))` resource right after a write sees the same stale state. Templates rarely see it, because effects run before views refresh.

**Example.** A username field whose async check has already reported `taken` for the current value:

```ts
import {Component, resource, signal} from '@angular/core';
import {form, FormField, submit, validateAsync} from '@angular/forms/signals';

@Component({
  selector: 'username-form',
  imports: [FormField],
  template: `<input [formField]="f.username" />`,
})
export class UsernameForm {
  readonly f = form(signal({username: 'taken-name'}), (p) => {
    validateAsync(p.username, {
      params: ({value}) => value(),
      debounce: 300,
      factory: (username) =>
        resource({
          params: username,
          loader: ({params}) => fetch(`/api/username-available?u=${params}`).then((r) => r.json()),
        }),
      onSuccess: (available) => (available ? undefined : {kind: 'taken'}),
      onError: () => undefined,
    });
  });

  // Called from a keyboard shortcut, or the same thing happens through a WebMCP tool call.
  async useSuggestedName() {
    this.f.username().value.set('free-name');
    await submit(this.f, async () => {
      // Save the form.
    });
  }
}
```

**Current behavior,** right after `value.set('free-name')`:

```text
pending()   false
invalid()   true    (the 'taken' error for 'taken-name')
submit()    doesn't run the action
```

**Expected behavior (my assumption):**

```text
pending()   true
invalid()   false
submit()    runs the action, as it does for the same validator without debounce
```

This assumes that a debounced validator should behave like one without `debounce`, except for the delay before it runs. The `debounced()` guide supports that: it says that `status()` "tells you whether a new value is still pending" ([`debounced.md`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7/adev/src/content/guide/signals/debounced.md?plain=1#L34)).

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

Failing specs in triage PR #71637, which changes no library code:

- Forms: [`validate_async_debounce_window.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/forms/signals/test/node/validate_async_debounce_window.spec.ts)
- Core: [`debounce_status_spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/core/test/resource/debounce_status_spec.ts)

```bash
pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_arg=--filter="validateAsync debounce window" --test_output=all
pnpm bazel test //packages/core/test/resource:resource --test_arg=--filter="debounced status before effects run" --test_output=all
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

There's no error. The specs fail with:

```text
validateAsync debounce window with debounce: a value change is pending at once and submit() isn't blocked
    state read synchronously after value.set():
        Expected $.pending = false to equal true.
        Expected $.invalid = true to equal false.
    submit() ran the action for the new VALID value: Expected false to be true.
debounced status before effects run reports loading as soon as the source changes
    state right after source.set(): Expected $.status = 'resolved' to equal 'loading'.
debounced status before effects run makes a chained resource report loading as soon as the source changes
    chained resource status right after source.set(): Expected 'resolved' to be 'loading'.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
angular/angular main at 6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7 (2026-10-26), built from source
Test targets: //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test and //packages/core/test/resource:resource
OS: macOS (darwin arm64)
```

### Anything else?

**Affected areas:**

- `validateAsync()` and `validateHttp()` with `debounce`, when state is read or `submit()` is called in the same task as the write.
- WebMCP tool calls on signal forms with debounced async validators.
- Any app code that reads a `chain(debounced(...))` resource right after the source changes.
- Not affected: async validators without `debounce`, and templates, which render after effects run.

**Related work.** #70884 is about the same `chain(debounced(...))` wrapper in `validateAsync()`. #71414 tries to fix #70884 in forms, but it's stuck: the [review on Oct 25](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71414#pullrequestreview-5640773489) requested changes, and said that the gap isn't specific to signal forms and that keeping the previous settled value while debouncing causes stale results. #71414 also doesn't fix this window. The fix I recommend follows that review: it changes `debounced()` in core.

**Fix options and tradeoffs.** The PR has code for each option.

| Option | What changes | Tradeoffs |
|--------|--------------|-----------|
| A (recommended): `debounced()` reports `loading` as soon as its source changes | The `linkedSignal` in `debounced()` returns `loading` with the previous value when the source changes, and the effect checks whether a wait is active | Fixes every `chain(debounced(...))` user. With it applied, the specs and the core resource and signal forms suites pass. Synchronous `wait` functions show `loading` until effects flush. Factories with the #70884 pattern throw as soon as the value changes, instead of after effects run |
| B: `validateAsync()` treats a params mismatch as pending | Throw the `LOADING` marker while the debounced value differs from the params | Forms only. Needs a new private export from core |
| C: WebMCP waits for the app to be stable before submitting | One `await` in WebMCP's `execute` | Mitigation only. Other code that reads `pending()` right after a write still sees the old result |

**Where to look in the code:**

- [`validateAsync()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7/packages/forms/signals/src/api/rules/validation/validate_async.ts#L137-L141) wraps the params in `ɵchain(debounced(...))`.
- [`debounced()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7/packages/core/src/resource/debounce.ts#L80-L85) keeps its previous state when the source changes, and only its effect moves it to `loading`.
- The [triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/forms/signals/triage/debounce-pending-window.md) has the root cause, the measurements, and the full code for each option.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? forms ### Is this a regression? No ### Description **In short.** A form built with `compatForm()` can be invalid because of a `FormControl` validator, while its `errorSummary()` is empty. The errors also have no `fieldTree`, although their type says they do. **Why it matters.** `errorSummary()` is how an app lists every error at once, for example next to the submit button. With compat fields, `submit()` is blocked but the list is empty, so the user can't tell what to fix. Code that follows an error to its field, such as `error.fieldTree().focusBoundControl()`, throws on a compat error. **Failure mode in user code.** ```ts @Component({ imports: [FormField], template: ` @if (showErrors()) {
    @for (error of f().errorSummary(); track error) {
  • {{ error.kind }}
    • }
} `, }) export class Signup { readonly showErrors = signal(false); readonly model = signal({ name: new FormControl('', {nonNullable: true, validators: Validators.required}), }); readonly f = compatForm(this.model); save() { submit(this.f, { action: async () => saveSignup(this.model().name.value), onInvalid: () => this.showErrors.set(true), }); } } ``` Starting state: the `FormControl` value is `''`. `f.name().errors()` holds one `required` error, and `f().invalid()` is `true`. Current behavior: ```text 1. User clicks Save the action doesn't run; onInvalid shows the list f().errorSummary() → [] the list is empty ``` Expected behavior: ```text 1. User clicks Save the action doesn't run; onInvalid shows the list f().errorSummary() → [{kind: 'required', fieldTree: f.name}] the list shows "required" ``` **Assumptions: expected vs current.** | Expected | Current | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `errorSummary()` holds "the errors of the field and its descendants", as its doc comment says. | A compat field's `errorSummary` is a shared empty signal. | | `invalid()` and `errorSummary()` agree: an invalid form has at least one error in its summary. | `f().invalid()` is `true` while `f().errorSummary()` is `[]`. | | Every error typed `ValidationError.WithFieldTree` has a `fieldTree` that points at its field, as plain errors do. | `CompatValidationError` declares `fieldTree` but never sets it. | **Affected areas.** - `CompatValidationState` in `packages/forms/signals/compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts`: `errorSummary` and `errors`. - `CompatValidationError` in `packages/forms/signals/src/compat/validation_errors.ts`. - `errorSummary()` on any form with compat fields, including its DOM-order sort. - Consumers that read `error.fieldTree` on compat errors. **Tradeoffs of the fix.** - The summary fix needs `fieldTree` first. On the client, the root summary sorts errors by DOM position through `error.fieldTree()`, so adding compat errors without it would throw a `TypeError` once the summary has two or more errors. - Setting `fieldTree` in `CompatValidationState` with the existing `addDefaultField()` helper keeps the public `CompatValidationError` class unchanged. Adding a constructor parameter instead changes public API. - Nested errors of a `FormGroup` or `FormArray` value all point at the compat field, because nested controls have no `FieldTree` of their own. - A compat field bound with `[formControl]` instead of `[formField]` has no bound element, so its errors sort to the end of the summary. **Related.** #71633, where compat fields drop parse errors, changes the same class. **Details.** - Triage PR with the recommended fix, design decisions, and questions: #71630 - [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/df91c393eb29637719c4f8bcd5608fbaf23d6092/packages/forms/signals/triage/compat-error-summary.md): observed output, root cause, and the sort hazard. - [`CompatValidationState.errorSummary`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts#L55-L56), [`FieldValidationState.errorSummary`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/validation.ts#L275-L288), [`CompatValidationError`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/compat/validation_errors.ts#L19-L31), [`addDefaultField()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/validation.ts#L394-L414), [DOM-order sort](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/validation.ts#L416-L444). ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug [`compat_error_summary.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/df91c393eb29637719c4f8bcd5608fbaf23d6092/packages/forms/signals/test/node/compat/compat_error_summary.spec.ts) in the triage PR. Each spec asserts the expected behavior, so 2 of them fail today: ```bash pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_output=all ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```text No error is thrown. The repro specs report: root errorSummary(): Expected $.length = 0 to equal 1. fieldTree of the compat field error: Expected undefined to be Function. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```text angular/angular main at ce30bb0889 (2026-10-16), Bazel target //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test. The affected source files are unchanged on main at 3e173fc844 (2026-10-24). ``` ### Anything else? I searched for an existing issue or PR and found none.

Issues.Title: Signal forms: compatForm() fields ignore parse errors, so submit() sends the last valid value
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? forms ### Is this a regression? No ### Description **In short.** When a `compatForm()` field is bound with `[formField]` to a control that can't parse what the user typed, the field ignores the parse error. For example, `` with `30e` in it. The field stays valid, no error shows, and `submit()` runs with the last value that parsed. The same template on a plain `form()` field blocks the submit. **Why it matters.** `compatForm()` is the documented way to migrate a reactive form to signal forms step by step, and the [migration guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/migration.md?plain=1#L46-L76) binds compat fields with `[formField]`. The failure is silent: the user sees one value, and the app saves another. **Failure mode in user code.** ```ts @Component({ imports: [FormField], template: ` @if (f.age().invalid()) {

Enter a valid age.

} `, }) export class Profile { readonly model = signal({age: new FormControl(30, {nonNullable: true})}); readonly f = compatForm(this.model); save() { submit(this.f, async () => { await saveProfile({age: this.model().age.value}); }); } } ``` Starting state: the `FormControl` value is `30`, the input shows `30`, `f.age().errors()` is `[]`, and `f.age().invalid()` is `false`. Current behavior: ```text 1. User types "30e" input shows "30e"; FormControl value stays 30 f.age().errors() → [] f.age().invalid() → false no error message 2. User clicks Save the action runs and saves {age: 30} ``` Expected behavior: ```text 1. User types "30e" input shows "30e"; FormControl value stays 30 f.age().errors() → [{kind: 'parse', ...}] f.age().invalid() → true "Enter a valid age." shows 2. User clicks Save the action doesn't run ``` **Assumptions: expected vs current.** | Expected | Current | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | A compat field reports its controls' parse errors like a plain field does: in `errors()`, in `invalid()`, and at the submit gate. | `CompatValidationState.parseErrors` is hardcoded to `[]`. | | The `FormControl`'s own state still shows through ("Reactive state is proxied automatically" in the guide). Parse errors add to it. | `errors`, `valid`, `invalid`, and `syncValid` come only from the `FormControl`. | | The control that reported the parse error can show it. | `FormField.errors()` filters the field's `errors()`, so the binding's own errors are empty too. | **Affected areas.** - `CompatValidationState` in `packages/forms/signals/compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts`: `parseErrors`, `errors`, `syncValid`, `valid`, and `invalid`. - Every source of parse errors, on a compat field: - Native inputs with bad input, such as number, date, and time. - Legacy `NG_VALIDATORS` on a CVA, which are shimmed into parse errors. - Custom controls that report `parseErrors`. - `submit()` on a compat root, and on a plain root with compat children. - The migration guide's statements that reactive state is proxied and that `errors()` returns `CompatValidationError`. **Tradeoffs of the fix.** - After the fix, `f.age().invalid()` is `true` while the `FormControl` and its parent `FormGroup` still report valid. Parse errors live in the signal-forms layer, so reactive code that checks `formGroup.valid` disagrees with `submit()`. - Writing parse errors into the `FormControl` with `setErrors()` would avoid that split, but the next `updateValueAndValidity()` wipes them, and it fights reactive forms' ownership of the control. - `errors()` would mix `CompatValidationError` with parse errors, which have no `control` or `context`. The public type doesn't change, and the guide's `errorMessage()` helper on `main` already falls back to `error.message ?? error.kind`. - Only documenting the limitation is cheapest, but it leaves a silent submit with the wrong value. For comparison, the two APIs that compat bridges both catch this case. Reactive forms' `NumberValueAccessor` writes `null` for bad input, so `Validators.required` fails. Plain signal forms block the submit. **Related bug, same file.** A compat field's `errorSummary` is always empty, so the root's `errorSummary()` omits every `FormControl` error: #71634. **Details.** - Triage PR with the recommended fix, design decisions, and questions: #71628 - [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/9a747b865e1f4725fde103a947f5308ce8d1b365/packages/forms/signals/triage/compat-parse-errors.md): observed output, root cause, and history. - [`CompatValidationState`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts#L26-L75), [`FieldValidationState.parseErrors` and `errors`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/validation.ts#L258-L273), [`FormField.errors`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/form_field.ts#L196-L202), [`submit()` gate](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/api/structure.ts#L528-L540), [`errorMessage()` in the guide on `main`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/migration.md?plain=1#L79-L91). ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug [`compat_parse_errors.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/9a747b865e1f4725fde103a947f5308ce8d1b365/packages/forms/signals/test/web/compat_parse_errors.spec.ts) in the triage PR. The repro spec asserts the expected behavior and fails today. The web test runner ignores `--filter`, so this runs the whole Chromium suite: ```bash pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_chromium --test_output=all ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```text No error is thrown. The repro spec reports: Expected $.fieldErrors.length = 0 to equal 1. Expected $.fieldInvalid = false to equal true. Expected $.rootInvalid = false to equal true. Unexpected $.actionSaw[0] = 5 in array. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```text angular/angular main at ce30bb0889 (2026-10-16), Bazel target //packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_chromium. The affected source files are unchanged on main at 3e173fc844 (2026-10-24). Native inputs have produced parse errors since v22.0.0-next.0. ``` ### Anything else? I searched for an existing issue or PR and found none.
