Issues.Title: Signal forms: a parse error on one control shows up on every other control bound to the same field
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

**In short.** When one field is bound to several controls and one of them has a parse error, CVA and
native hosts receive that parse error in their `errors` too. So does `NgControl.errors`. Each
control should receive only the parse errors it produced, as custom controls do today.

**Why it matters.** Binding one field to two controls is a common pattern, for example a slider
next to a number input. Typing `5e` into the number input then makes the slider show the number
input's parse error as its own. Parse errors became common in v22: native inputs produce them, and so do
legacy CVA validators.

**Failure mode in user code.**

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-slider',
  template: `
    <input type="range" min="0" max="100" />
    @for (error of errors(); track error) {
      <small>{{ error.message ?? error.kind }}</small>
    }
  `,
  providers: [{provide: NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR, useExisting: Slider, multi: true}],
})
export class Slider implements ControlValueAccessor {
  readonly errors = input<readonly ValidationError[]>([]);
  // writeValue, registerOnChange, and registerOnTouched omitted.
}

@Component({
  imports: [FormField, Slider],
  template: `
    <app-slider [formField]="f.volume" />
    <input type="number" [formField]="f.volume" />
  `,
})
export class Mixer {
  readonly f = form(signal({volume: 50}));
}
```

Starting state: `f.volume().value()` is `50`, both controls show `50`, and neither has errors.

Current behavior:

```text
1. User types "5e" into the number input
   number input  FormField.errors() → [{kind: 'parse'}]
   slider        errors input       → [{kind: 'parse'}]   the slider shows the error
   both          invalid input      → true
```

Expected behavior:

```text
1. User types "5e" into the number input
   number input  FormField.errors() → [{kind: 'parse'}]
   slider        errors input       → []                  the slider shows nothing
   both          invalid input      → true
```

**History.** The filter existed for every host in v21.2.0-next.1
([`ebae211add`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ebae211add37700858adeb8fc5d87bf503a59721)).
The refactor in v21.2.0-next.2
([`a67e00741c`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/a67e00741c23d7ae4c93970c026bd7f9d41521ee))
kept it only for custom controls. The leak became visible in v22.0.0-next.0, when native inputs
started producing parse errors
([`22afbb2f36`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/22afbb2f36be89c2ae575df343571a918dec5985)).

**Assumptions: expected vs current.**

| Expected                                                                                                                         | Current                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Each control receives only the parse errors of its own binding. `ebae211add` states this, and custom controls still work this way. | CVA and native hosts receive the field's unfiltered `errors()`.           |
| `inject(NgControl).errors` reflects the binding it was injected for.                                                              | It converts the field's unfiltered `errors()`.                             |
| `invalid` is field-level, so every control on the field receives `true`.                                                          | Same. This doesn't change.                                                 |

**Affected areas.**

- `readFieldStateBindingValue()` in `packages/forms/signals/src/directive/bindings.ts`, and its
  callers in `control_cva.ts`, `control_native.ts`, and `control_custom.ts`.
- `InteropNgControl.errors` in `packages/forms/signals/src/controls/interop_ng_control.ts`, and how
  `FormField` creates it.
- Consumers: directives with an `errors` input on native elements, CVA components with an `errors`
  input, and components that read `NgControl.errors`.
- Not affected: `FormField.errors()`, which is already filtered, and custom controls.

**Tradeoffs of the fix.**

- Routing every host through one helper that reads `FormField.errors` changes an internal
  function's signature and its three callers. Copying the special case into two more files is a
  smaller diff, but three copies are how the behavior drifted.
- Filtering `NgControl.errors` means passing the binding's errors into `InteropNgControl`, which is
  an internal constructor change. It can land with the fix or later.
- A control can receive `invalid: true` with empty `errors`. Custom controls already get that
  today, so UI that shows invalid styling without a message stays as it is.

**Details.**

- Triage PR with the recommended fix, design decisions, and questions: #71629
- [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/7e43a71da8e7763a078ac5c4dbbe0d847ef52efa/packages/forms/signals/triage/errors-per-control.md):
  observed output, history, and the `NgControl` path.
- [Custom host, filtered](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/control_custom.ts#L41-L45),
  [CVA host](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/control_cva.ts#L99-L101),
  [native host](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/control_native.ts#L113-L114),
  [`readFieldStateBindingValue()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/bindings.ts#L58-L64),
  [`InteropNgControl.errors`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/controls/interop_ng_control.ts#L93-L95).

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

[`form_field_errors_per_binding.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/7e43a71da8e7763a078ac5c4dbbe0d847ef52efa/packages/forms/signals/test/web/form_field_errors_per_binding.spec.ts)
in the triage PR. Both specs assert the expected behavior and fail today. The web test runner
ignores `--filter`, so this runs the whole Chromium suite:

```bash
pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_chromium --test_output=all
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```text
No error is thrown. The repro specs report:

Unexpected $[1].errorsInput[0] = 'parse from native (bad input)' in array.
Unexpected $[2].errorsInput[0] = 'parse from native (bad input)' in array.
Unexpected $[1].errors[0] = 'parse' in array.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
angular/angular main at ce30bb0889 (2026-10-16), Bazel target
//packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_chromium. The affected source files are unchanged on main at
3e173fc844 (2026-10-24). First affected prerelease: v21.2.0-next.2.
```

### Anything else?

Issues.Title: Signal forms: a custom debouncer's abort listener runs late, inside a computation
Issues.Body: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? forms ### Is this a regression? No ### Description **In short.** Signal forms pass an `AbortSignal` to a custom debouncer. It should fire when the user moves on before the debounce finishes. Today it fires at the wrong time, and its listeners run inside a `linkedSignal` computation. An abort listener that touches a signal breaks: - Writing a signal throws NG0600, so the write is lost. - Reading a signal can make the form drop the value the user typed. - A debounce that already finished is aborted on the next blur, so the listener runs anyway. **Why it matters.** The obvious use of a custom debouncer is a "searching" indicator, and its abort listener writes a signal. In such an app, every blur after a finished debounce logs NG0600, and a programmatic model write can leave the indicator stuck on. The built-in debouncers, `debounce(path, ms)` and `debounce(path, 'blur')`, aren't affected. **Failure mode in user code.** ```ts @Component({ imports: [FormField], template: ` @if (searching()) { Searching… } `, }) export class Search { readonly searching = signal(false); readonly model = signal({query: ''}); readonly f = form(this.model, (p) => { debounce(p.query, (_ctx, abortSignal) => { this.searching.set(true); return new Promise((resolve) => { const timer = setTimeout(() => { this.searching.set(false); resolve(); }, 300); abortSignal.addEventListener('abort', () => { clearTimeout(timer); this.searching.set(false); resolve(); }); }); }); }); } ``` Starting state: `model().query` is `''`, `searching()` is `false`, and no debounce is pending. Current behavior: ```text 1. User types "ng" searching() → true, model().query → '' (debounce pending) 2. 300 ms pass searching() → false, model().query → 'ng' (debounce finished) 3. User tabs out (blur) the finished debounce is aborted; the listener's searching.set(false) throws NG0600: Writing to signals is not allowed in a `computed`. The error is reported as uncaught. ``` Expected behavior: ```text 1. User types "ng" searching() → true, model().query → '' (debounce pending) 2. 300 ms pass searching() → false, model().query → 'ng' (debounce finished) 3. User tabs out (blur) nothing to abort; no error ``` Two more failure modes, each covered by a repro spec: - **Stuck indicator.** Type "ng", then set `model` in code, for example in an Escape key handler, and blur before 300 ms pass. The listener clears the timer, then throws on `searching.set(false)` before `resolve()`. `searching()` stays `true`. - **Lost value.** If an abort listener reads a signal while it runs inside the computation, that signal becomes a dependency of the internal `pendingSync`. When it changes, the next read aborts the *live* debounce. The input shows what the user typed, but the model keeps the old value after blur. **Assumptions: expected vs current.** | Expected (from the docs and the code's own comments) | Current | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | The abort fires when the value changes before the debounce resolves (guide, `pendingSync` doc comment). | A direct model write only marks `pendingSync` dirty. The abort fires at the next keystroke, touch, or reset. | | A debounce that finished is never aborted. | The finished controller stays in `pendingSync` and is aborted at the next read. | | Abort listeners run like any event listener, outside a reactive context, so they can read and write signals. | They run inside the `linkedSignal` computation, with dependency tracking on. | **Affected areas.** - `FieldNode` in `packages/forms/signals/src/field/node.ts`: `pendingSync`, `debounceSync()`, `flushSync()`, and `_reset()`. - Custom debouncers passed to `debounce(path, fn)` whose abort listeners read or write signals. - The guide's description of the abort timing in `async-operations.md`. - Tests: an NG0600 caught by `dispatchEvent` surfaces as an uncaught error and can fail an unrelated spec that runs later. **Tradeoffs of the fix.** - The recommended fix keeps today's timing for direct model writes and rewords the guide. An immediate abort needs an `effect` per debounced field, and effects run asynchronously anyway. - Replacing the `linkedSignal` with a plain field removes one `linkedSignal` from every field, debounced or not. It changes one flow: touching after a direct write now reaches `sync()`. That's a no-op for plain fields, but on a `compatForm()` field it calls `FormControl.setValue()` and emits `valueChanges` again, unless the fix also skips that `sync()`. - Keeping the `linkedSignal` gives a smaller diff, but user listeners still run during a computation. **Details.** - Triage PR with the recommended fix, design decisions, and questions: #71627 - [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/c1bcad6ef84ba8e5a6ed7d269df186ba4901194a/packages/forms/signals/triage/debounce-abort-signal.md): observed output, root cause, and the measured fix options. - [`pendingSync`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/node.ts#L140-L152), [`flushSync()` and `debounceSync()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/node.ts#L413-L447), [`linkedSignal` computation](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/core/primitives/signals/src/linked_signal.ts#L156-L178), [guide text](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/async-operations.md?plain=1#L472), [built-in debouncers](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/api/rules/debounce.ts#L64-L94). ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug [`debounce_abort.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/c1bcad6ef84ba8e5a6ed7d269df186ba4901194a/packages/forms/signals/test/node/debounce_abort.spec.ts) in the triage PR. Each spec asserts the expected behavior, so 6 of them fail today: ```bash pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_output=all ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```text Error: NG0600: Writing to signals is not allowed in a `computed`. Signal: 'debouncing'. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```text angular/angular main at ce30bb0889 (2026-10-16), Bazel target //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test. The affected source files are unchanged on main at 3e173fc844 (2026-10-24). ``` ### Anything else? I searched for an existing issue or PR and found none.

Issues.Title: Signal forms: `required()`, `min()`, and other built-in rules create an injector for every field
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

In a signal form, each field can get its own injector, so that a managed metadata key, like the one `validateAsync()` uses, can create resources in the field's injection context. But today a field creates an injector as soon as it has **any** metadata rule. Most built-in rules add metadata, so `required()`, `min()`, `max()`, `minLength()`, `maxLength()`, `minDate()`, `maxDate()`, `pattern()`, `validateStandardSchema()`, and `debounce()` all give each field an injector that nothing uses.

Removing a field also creates an injector if it didn't have one, just so the cleanup can destroy it.

**Why it matters.** The cost grows with the number of fields. Large tables, line-item lists, and dynamic arrays usually put `required()` or `min()` on every row. Each injector took about 1.1 to 1.5 µs to create in my measurement, and it also holds memory, which I didn't measure. This doesn't break anything, but it's work that the feature doesn't need.

**Example.** An order form with 1,000 line items:

```ts
import {Component, signal} from '@angular/core';
import {applyEach, form, FormField, min, required} from '@angular/forms/signals';

@Component({
  selector: 'order-lines',
  imports: [FormField],
  template: `
    @for (line of f; track $index) {
      <input [formField]="line.sku" />
      <input type="number" [formField]="line.qty" />
    }
  `,
})
export class OrderLines {
  readonly lines = signal(Array.from({length: 1000}, () => ({sku: '', qty: 1})));
  readonly f = form(this.lines, (p) => {
    applyEach(p, (line) => {
      required(line.sku);
      min(line.qty, 1);
    });
  });
}
```

**Current behavior:**

```text
read every line's fields, as the template does   → 2,000 injectors (one per sku field, one per qty field)
lines.set([])                                    → 1,000 more injectors (one per line, created only to be destroyed)
```

**Expected behavior (my assumption):**

```text
read every line's fields, as the template does   → 0 injectors (neither rule needs an injection context)
lines.set([])                                    → 0 injectors
```

This assumes that only managed metadata keys need a field injector. That's what the [field metadata guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/field-metadata.md?plain=1#L314) documents: a managed key's `create` runs in the field's injection context. Plain metadata keys only compute a value. Fields with `validateAsync()` or `validateHttp()` would still get an injector.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

Failing specs: [`field_injector_allocation.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-injector-allocation/packages/forms/signals/test/node/field_injector_allocation.spec.ts) in triage PR #71626. The PR changes no library code.

```bash
pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_arg=--filter="field injector allocation" --test_output=all
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

There's no error. The specs count `Injector.create` calls for 50 array items with one rule each. They fail with:

```text
creates injectors only for fields with managed metadata keys (50 items per rule)
    Expected $.required = 50 to equal 0.
    Expected $.min = 50 to equal 0.
    Expected $.debounce = 50 to equal 0.
creates no injectors to destroy 50 removed fields that never had one
    Injector.create calls while the cleanup sweep destroys the removed items: Expected 50 to be 0.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
angular/angular main at 3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5 (2026-10-24), built from source
Test target: //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test
OS: macOS (darwin arm64)
```

### Anything else?

**Affected areas:**

- Fields with any of these rules: `required()`, `min()`, `max()`, `minLength()`, `maxLength()`, `minDate()`, `maxDate()`, `pattern()`, `validateStandardSchema()`, and `debounce()`.
- Fields with custom `metadata()` rules that use plain keys from `createMetadataKey()`.
- Removing any field that never had an injector, including fields with no rules.
- Combined with #70627, where the cleanup sweep materializes every reachable field, every field with one of these rules gets an injector after the first sweep, even if nothing reads it. I found this by reading the code, and no spec checks it.
- Not affected: fields with no rules, or with `validate()` only. Fields with `validateAsync()` or `validateHttp()` need their injector and keep it.

**Fix options and tradeoffs.** The PR has code for each option.

| Option | What changes | Tradeoffs |
|--------|--------------|-----------|
| A (recommended): create the injector only for managed keys | Move `runInInjectionContext()` inside the check for `key.create`, and don't create an injector during cleanup | Small change, same documented contract. A field with several managed keys enters the injection context once per key |
| B: cache a "has managed keys" flag on the schema logic | Return early before touching the injector | Also skips a loop per field, but the cached flag could go stale, because metadata keys are added lazily |
| C: replace field injectors with a lightweight scope | Shared with the host teardown issue (#71622) | Cheapest per field, but a much larger change |

**Where to look in the code:**

- [`runMetadataCreateLifecycle()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/packages/forms/signals/src/field/metadata.ts#L34-L58) enters the field's injection context before it checks whether any key needs it.
- [`FieldNodeStructure.destroy()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/packages/forms/signals/src/field/structure.ts#L216-L218) reads the lazy `injector` getter, which creates an injector if there wasn't one.
- The [triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-injector-allocation/packages/forms/signals/triage/injector-allocation.md) has the counts for each rule, the root cause, and the full code for each option.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): support resolving subproject dependencies in bun workspaces
Issues.Body:
When running `bun pm ls` inside a workspace member directory, Bun resolves the workspace root lockfile and outputs only the direct dependencies declared in the root `package.json`, along with `workspace:` references to member packages. Because subproject dependencies (such as `@angular/core`) are omitted from this output, commands like `ng update` and `ng add` fail to detect installed project dependencies when executed in a Bun workspace member.

To resolve this, `parseBunDependencies` now ignores `workspace:` protocol entries, and the `bun` package manager descriptor enables `requiresManifestDependencyLookup`. When populating the dependency cache, `PackageManager` supplements the command output by reading `dependencies` and `devDependencies` from the working directory's `package.json` and resolving their installed manifests across ancestor `node_modules` directories up to the workspace lockfile or repository root. Additionally, `getPackageNameCommand` is configured for `bun` using `bun pm pkg get name` to provide the same CLI fallback as `npm` and `pnpm`.

Fixes #34402

Issues.Title: Server build bundles two copies of Domino, so DOM globals from `init` and the `DominoAdapter` are different classes
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

Not a regression. The second copy appeared when the dedicated `polyfills.server` bundle was introduced in v17 and has been there since.

### Description

With `outputMode: 'server'` (the default `ng new --ssr` setup), `@angular/build:application` emits two complete copies of Domino into the server output, and both are evaluated in the same Node process:

| File | Brings in Domino via |
|---|---|
| `polyfills.server.mjs` | `@angular/platform-server/init`, pushed unconditionally in `createServerPolyfillBundleOptions` ([application-code-bundle.ts#L184](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/application-code-bundle.ts#L184)) |
| `main.server.mjs` | `@angular/platform-server` itself (`DominoAdapter`) |

The two bundles are separate esbuild contexts, so the `third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` module that both entry points import is inlined into each output. `main.server.mjs` starts with `import './polyfills.server.mjs'`, so both copies load.

#### The two copies are different class hierarchies

`platform-server` runs the same shim as `init` in `DominoAdapter.makeCurrent()` → `setDomTypes()` during `PLATFORM_INITIALIZER`, using *its* copy. So on the first render every global that `init` set is overwritten by the second copy. Any code that captured a DOM class at module-evaluation time, which is exactly the scenario `init` exists to support, then holds a class from the other hierarchy:

```ts
// top of some module (e.g. a library doing `class Foo extends HTMLElement`)
const Captured = HTMLElement;                   // Domino copy #1, from polyfills.server.mjs

// later, during rendering
inject(DOCUMENT).body instanceof Captured;      // false  (body is from copy #2)
inject(DOCUMENT).body instanceof HTMLElement;   // true   (global was overwritten)
Captured === HTMLElement;                       // false
```

#### Measured cost of the second copy

Default `ng new --ssr` app, Angular CLI 22.2.4, `@angular/build` 22.2.4, `@angular/platform-server` 22.2.3, Node 26.8.1. "Without" is the same build with `@angular/platform-server/init` removed from the server polyfills and nothing else changed. Memory is the median over 11 fresh processes per variant, forced GC before each snapshot, after serving 50 SSR requests.

| | With `init` (default) | Without | Cost of the extra copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `polyfills.server.mjs` on disk | 235.58 kB | 128 B | **235 kB** |
| Retained V8 heap after loading `main.server.mjs` | 3,875 KB | 2,739 KB | **~1.1 MB** |
| Retained V8 heap after 50 requests | 12,477 KB | 11,342 KB | **~1.1 MB** (does not grow) |
| Import time of `polyfills.server.mjs` | ~7.5 ms | ~0.6 ms | **~7 ms** startup |
| Prerendered / SSR HTML | identical | identical | — |

The 1.1 MB is permanent: the ESM module namespace keeps every Domino function and prototype reachable for the lifetime of the process. From a heap-snapshot diff it is roughly 350 KB compiled code and function metadata, 340 KB retained source strings, 200 KB prototype and lookup tables, 110 KB function objects, and V8 internals for the rest. The `Object.assign(globalThis, domino.impl)` itself is negligible (95 properties, ~7 KB, 0.03 ms); the cost is the second module evaluation.

To be clear about scale: in a fresh default app the duplicate is about 30% of the retained heap after loading the server bundles and about 2% of process RSS once requests are served. Small in absolute terms, but pure overhead on every SSR deployment, and the `instanceof` inconsistency above comes with it.

### Minimal Reproduction

```bash
npx @angular/cli@22.2.4 new repro --ssr --defaults
cd repro
npx ng build --configuration development   # keeps esbuild's module markers
grep -n "^// node_modules/@angular/platform-server" dist/repro/server/*.mjs
```

Actual:

```
main.server.mjs:36143:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs
main.server.mjs:52859:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/_server-chunk.mjs
main.server.mjs:53402:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/platform-server.mjs
polyfills.server.mjs:4:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs
polyfills.server.mjs:16720:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/init.mjs
```

Expected: `bundled-domino.mjs` appears once across the server output.

Full repro with the memory-measurement harness and the `instanceof` probe: https://github.com/ChristopherPHolder/ng-double-domino

### Exception or Error

```
(none; the build succeeds)
```

### Your Environment

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.4
Node.js           : 26.8.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0

@angular/build            22.2.4
@angular/core             22.2.3
@angular/platform-server  22.2.3
@angular/ssr              22.2.4
```

### Anything else relevant?

#### Proposed fix (no API change), PR to follow

The polyfills bundle has to stay a separate, externally imported file: it is the only thing that guarantees `zone.js` and `init` evaluate before application code. (With code splitting, a side-effect import at the top of the `main.server` entry is inlined into the entry file while shared chunks are hoisted above it, so moving the `init` import there runs it *after* shared app chunks.) So the fix shares the copy rather than moving it:

- `polyfills.server.mjs` additionally re-exports the Domino module it already bundles via `init`.
- The main server bundle redirects `@angular/platform-server`'s `../third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` import to that export. `./polyfills.server.mjs` is already in `SERVER_GENERATED_EXTERNALS`, so this becomes a plain external import.

Verified on the repro above with the patched builder:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bundled-domino.mjs` in `main.server.mjs` | yes | no |
| `main.server.mjs` (production) | 537 kB | 301 kB |
| Retained heap after loading `main.server.mjs` | 3,875 KB | 2,831 KB |
| `body instanceof capturedHTMLElement` / `captured === HTMLElement` | false / false | true / true |
| SSR response | 200, 22,064 B | 200, 22,064 B |

It covers `outputMode: 'server'`, the legacy `ssr` + `prerender` path (same esbuild context, same banner), `platform: 'neutral'`, prerendering, and the dev server when bundling. When packages are external (`ng serve` prebundling) nothing changes, and Node's module cache already shares one copy there. The change comes with a spec under `builders/application/tests/behavior/`; today no spec or e2e asserts anything about `polyfills.server.mjs`.

#### Related

This fix keeps `@angular/platform-server/init` in every server build. Whether it should be there at all, and the lack of any user control over the server polyfills list, is a separate request: #34515.

<details>
<summary>How the duplicate came about</summary>

- **angular/angular#40559 (v12, 2021)** — `@angular/platform-server/init` created so DOM globals are available *before* platform init.
- **angular-cli `1199205bc` (v12)** — `universal` schematic adds the import to `main.server.ts`.
- **angular-cli `979bce45e` (v15)** — webpack server builder auto-adds it, removing the schematic import. `f143171fd` gates it on `@angular/platform-server` being installed (#24188).
- **angular-cli `095f5aba6` / `7defb3635` (v16)** — esbuild server bundling imports it in the virtual `main.server` entry; one copy.
- **angular-cli `886cb3167` (v17)** — a separate `polyfills.server` bundle is created to control zone.js flag ordering for cleaner stack traces. `init` moves into it with the other server polyfills. This is where the second copy starts; the commit is about zone.js and does not mention it.
- **angular/angular#52342 (v17)** — the shared `setDomTypes` import between `init` and `platform-server` is removed so the CLI can skip the JS transformer on the polyfills bundle (angular-cli#26113). After this the two entry points share no module, which guarantees two copies when bundled separately.

So the duplicate was never a deliberate choice; it fell out of two independent build-performance changes.

</details>
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Server build bundles two copies of Domino, so DOM globals from `init` and the `DominoAdapter` are different classes" (#34514)

## PR Checklist

[✓] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
[✓] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

[ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
[ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
[ ] Build related changes
[ ] CI related changes
[ ] Documentation content changes
[ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When bundling an application with server-side rendering, Domino (~560 KB unminified) is bundled into both `polyfills.server.mjs` (via `@angular/platform-server/init`) and `main.server.mjs` (via `@angular/platform-server`).

## What is the new behavior?

Domino is bundled only once in `polyfills.server.mjs` and attached to `globalThis['ɵdomino']`. The main server bundle redirects Domino imports to this shared instance.

This replaces the redundant bundled copy of Domino in `main.server.mjs` without requiring manual filesystem probing or `additionalContent` parameter threading in polyfill options.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

[ ] Yes
[✓] No

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

`refactor-jasmine-vitest` turns `spy.calls.first()` into `vi.mocked(spy).mock.calls[0]`, which is argumnets array of first call, and keeps `.args` that follows it
So `expect(spy.calls.first().args[0]).toBe(1)` becomes `expect(vi.mocked(spy).mock.calls[0].args[0]).toBe(1)` and converted spec does not build with `ng test` (checked on 22.3.0-next.3):

```
✘ [ERROR] TS2339: Property 'args' does not exist on type '[id: number, flag?: boolean | undefined]'. [plugin angular-compiler]
```

Without type check it throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')`
`mostRecent().args` and `all()[i].args` (#33206) already drop `.args`, only `first()` was missed

## What is the new behavior?

`spy.calls.first().args` becomes `vi.mocked(spy).mock.calls[0]`, in same transformer that handles `mostRecent().args`
Same spec after conversion builds and passes with `ng test`
Two new cases in `jasmine-spy_spec.ts`, both fail on main

- [x] No

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

`trust-proxy-headers` migration collects only `server` option of `build` target
In workspace created by `ng new --ssr` on 21 that option is `src/main.server.ts`, and `new AngularNodeAppEngine()` is in `src/server.ts`, which is set in `ssr.entry`

So `ng update` from 21 prints `Migration completed (No changes made)` for this migration and `src/server.ts` keeps `new AngularNodeAppEngine()` without options
On 21 undefined `trustProxyHeaders` trusted `x-forwarded-host` and `x-forwarded-proto`, on 22 it trusts nothing (#32911), so after update default SSR app stops trusting these headers and only logs warning when they arrive, which is exactly what migration was ment to avoid

Existing spec cases pass only because test workspace has `server: '/server.ts'`, `ng new` does not create that layout

## What is the new behavior?

Migration also collects `ssr.entry` file from `build` target options and configurations, `server` is still collected for other layouts
On default SSR workspace `src/server.ts` gets TODO comment and `trustProxyHeaders: ['x-forwarded-host', 'x-forwarded-proto']`, `src/main.server.ts` is left as is

New case in `migration_spec.ts` uses real layout (`server: 'src/main.server.ts'`, `ssr.entry: 'src/server.ts'`), it fails on main

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Workspaces that already went to 22 can run it again once they are on release with this fix:

```
ng update @angular/cli --name trust-proxy-headers
```

Issues.Title: ci: update e2e runs-on to ubuntu-24.04
Issues.Body:
The `ubuntu-latest` runner image recently began migrating to Ubuntu 26.04, which mounts `/tmp` as a 7.8 GB `tmpfs` RAM disk with a per-user disk quota. This causes large builds and package extraction (such as yarn in E2E tests) to fail with `EDQUOT` (disk quota exceeded).

See: https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14777

This commit pins `runs-on` to `ubuntu-24.04` for the E2E test jobs.

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #34514

The server build emits two complete copies of domino: `polyfills.server.mjs` bundles it via `@angular/platform-server/init`, and `main.server.mjs` bundles it again via `@angular/platform-server`. The two bundles are separate esbuild contexts, so the shared `third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` module is inlined into each, and both are evaluated at runtime (`main.server.mjs` imports `./polyfills.server.mjs` first).

Because the two copies are distinct class hierarchies, DOM globals captured at module-evaluation time (the scenario `init` exists for) do not match the classes the platform renders with:

```ts
const Captured = HTMLElement;              // polyfills.server.mjs copy
inject(DOCUMENT).body instanceof Captured; // false: body is from the main.server.mjs copy
```

## What is the new behavior?

<!-- Please describe the new behavior that. -->

The server polyfills bundle re-exports the domino module it already contains, and the main server bundle redirects the `@angular/platform-server` import of `../third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` to that export. `./polyfills.server.mjs` is already in `SERVER_GENERATED_EXTERNALS` and imported first by every server bundle, so the evaluation order is unchanged.

The polyfills bundle has to stay a separate, externally imported file: with code splitting, a side-effect import at the top of the `main.server` entry is inlined into the entry while shared chunks are hoisted above it, so moving the `init` import there would run it after shared application chunks. Sharing the copy avoids that.

On the default `ng new --ssr` app (Angular CLI 22.2.4, Node 26.8.1):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bundled-domino.mjs` in `main.server.mjs` | yes | no |
| `main.server.mjs` (production) | 537 kB | 301 kB |
| Retained V8 heap after loading `main.server.mjs` | 3,875 KB | 2,831 KB |
| `body instanceof capturedHTMLElement` | false | true |
| SSR response | 200, 22,064 B | 200, 22,064 B |

Covered: `outputMode: 'server'`, the legacy `ssr` + `prerender` path (same esbuild context and banner), `platform: 'neutral'`, prerendering, and the dev server when bundling. When packages are external (`ng serve` prebundling) nothing changes; Node's module cache already shares one copy there. If `@angular/platform-server` is not installed, is external, or has an unexpected layout, both sides fall back to today's behavior.

Reproduction with the measurement harness and the `instanceof` probe: https://github.com/ChristopherPHolder/ng-double-domino

## Other information

`@angular/platform-server/init` is still added to every server build. Making that optional (and the server polyfills list user-controllable in general) is a separate request: #34515.

### [`v8.12.2`](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/releases/tag/v8.12.2)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v8.12.1...v8.12.2)

##### Security fixes

##### High severity

##### Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

**CVE-2026-87018 · [GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm)**

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

##### TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped `Agent` options

**CVE-2026-109383 · [GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx)**

`Agent` used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as `checkServerIdentity`. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

##### Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

**CVE-2026-109829 · [GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26)**

When an originless `Agent` combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as `compose(redirect(), cache())`, a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

##### Denial of service through excessive `Content-Encoding` values

**CVE-2026-109869 · [GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c)**

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although `fetch()` rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

##### Medium severity

##### Denial of service through the `decompress` interceptor

**CVE-2026-87029 · [GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6)**

An exception thrown by a downstream response handler from an asynchronous decompression callback could escape as an uncaught exception. A server could trigger this when `decompress` was composed with a handler such as `dump` with a size limit. This release converts downstream handler exceptions into per-request errors.

##### Subresource Integrity bypass with non-lowercase algorithm tokens

**CVE-2026-109841 · [GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472)**

`fetch()` treated valid mixed-case or uppercase SRI algorithm tokens, such as `SHA256`, as unknown and could accept a response whose body did not match the configured digest. This release normalizes algorithm tokens before validation and digest selection.

##### Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

**CVE-2026-109924 · [GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685)**

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny `data:` fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

##### Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

**CVE-2026-109932 · [GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6)**

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v8.12.1...v8.12.2>

Issues.Title: @angular/build@21 depends on undici@7.29.1 which is vulnerable to multiple CVEs
Issues.Body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

@angular/build v21 depends on undici v7.29.1 which is vulnerable to CVE-2026-109924, CVE-2026-109841 and CVE-2026-109869. Fixed version is v7.30.1.
As far as I can tell, @angular/build v20 and v22 do not depend on undici at all and are therefore not affected.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. npm install @angular/build@21
2. npm audit

### Exception or Error

```text

```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 21.2.27
Angular           : 21.2.25
Node.js           : 24.22.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : linux x64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 21.2.27           │ ^21.2.27          │
│ @angular/cdk              │ 21.2.14           │ ^21.2.14          │
│ @angular/cli              │ 21.2.27           │ ^21.2.21          │
│ @angular/common           │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.20          │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.25          │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.25          │
│ @angular/core             │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.25          │
│ @angular/elements         │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.20          │
│ @angular/forms            │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.20          │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.20          │
│ @angular/router           │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.25          │
│ @angular/service-worker   │ 21.2.25           │ ^21.2.20          │
│ ng-packagr                │ 21.2.7            │ ^21.2             │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ^7.8.2            │
│ typescript                │ 5.9.3             │ ^5.9.3 || ^6      │
│ vitest                    │ 4.1.12            │ ^4.1.7            │
│ zone.js                   │ 0.16.3            │ ^0.15 || ^0.16    │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else relevant?

Since I open issues to update vulnerable dependencies fairly often now, I want to ask a few questions:
1. What is the reason for pinning versions in package.json? In this case doing a ~7.29.1 would not help, I know, but in many other cases it would.
2. Should there be some kind of security scanner, a scheduled GitHub action running `npm audit` or something similar? This would probably detect vulnerable dependencies way faster than I do.
3. The time to fix those vulnerable dependencies measured from release of the fix for the dependency until release of @angular/xxx is sometimes very long (> 1 week), which in my opinion is too much nowadays. This is my general concern and the first two questions already try to find solutions to this. Any other ideas?

Issues.Title: ssr: string redirectTo drops trailing slash in query and fragment
Issues.Body:
### Command

build, serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

none, same baseHref join is there since 19.0.0

### Description

String `redirectTo` loses trailing `/` of query or fragment in `Location`: `'/login?next=/a/'` gives `/login?next=/a` and `'/login#section/'` gives `/login#section`. Same with `X-Forwarded-Prefix` and with base href `/base/`, on 22.2.4 and on main snapshot `22.3.0-next.3+sha-928169a`

Function redirect with same target keeps it (`/login?next=%2Fa%2F` and `/login#section/`) since router serializes it, so same target gives diffrent `Location` depending only on how redirect is written

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `npx -p @angular/cli@latest ng new repro --ssr --defaults --skip-git`
2. `src/app/app.routes.ts`:

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

@Component({ template: 'login' })
class Login {}

export const routes: Routes = [
  { path: 'login', component: Login },
  { path: 'old', redirectTo: '/login?next=/a/' },
  { path: 'old-hash', redirectTo: '/login#section/' },
  { path: 'old-fn', redirectTo: () => '/login?next=/a/' },
  { path: 'old-fn-hash', redirectTo: () => '/login#section/' },
];
```

3. `src/app/app.routes.server.ts`: `[{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server }]` so function redirects go through render
4. `ng build` then `NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost NG_TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=x-forwarded-prefix node dist/repro/server/server.mjs`
5. curl:

```text
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old | grep -i '^location'
location: /login?next=/a
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /login#section
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-fn | grep -i '^location'
location: /login?next=%2Fa%2F
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-fn-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /login#section/
$ curl -si -H 'X-Forwarded-Prefix: /app' localhost:4000/old | grep -i '^location'
location: /app/login?next=/a
$ curl -si -H 'X-Forwarded-Prefix: /app' localhost:4000/old-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /app/login#section
```

With `ng build --base-href /base/` it's `/base/login?next=/a` and `/base/login#section`. Slash is gone already at build time, `dist/repro/server/angular-app-manifest.mjs` has `"redirectTo": "/login?next=/a"`

Issues.Title: build: ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE when loading oxc-parser in StackBlitz / WebContainer
Issues.Body:
### Command
build, serve

### Is this a regression?
Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### Description
In StackBlitz (WebContainer), running an Angular application with `@angular/build` fails during `ng serve` / `ng build` with:

```
(node:12) ExperimentalWarning: WASI is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
[oxc-parser] Downloading @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.150.0 on WebContainer...
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE]: Cannot require() ES Module /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle. (from /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/@angular/build/src/tools/oxc/oxc-transform.js) A cycle involving require(esm) is not allowed to maintain invariants mandated by the ECMAScript specification. Try making at least part of the dependency in the graph lazily loaded.
    at ModuleLoader.importSyncForRequire (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:169:3960)
    at loadESMFromCJS (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19002)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19068)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:20043)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17661)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:15179)
    at wrapModuleLoad (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:4199)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17842)
    at require2 (node:internal/modules/helpers:177:3126) {
  code: 'ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE'
}
```

Parent issue: https://github.com/stackblitz/starters/issues/136

#### Analysis & Root Cause

1. **No actual cyclic dependency in the code:**
   The module graph (`oxc-transform.ts` -> `oxc-parser`, `oxc-transform.ts` -> `traversal.ts` -> `oxc-parser`) is an acyclic DAG.
   The `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE` error is a known misleading error in Node.js's synchronous `require(esm)` loader (Node.js issues [#55516](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/55516) and [#57172](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/57172)). When an ES module throws an error during synchronous `require(esm)` evaluation, Node's loader frequently shadows the real underlying exception and reports that the module was required in a cycle.

2. **WebContainer Fallback Failure:**
   - StackBlitz WebContainer cannot run native `.node` addons.
   - `oxc-parser`'s `optionalDependencies` only list platform-specific native addons (`@oxc-parser/binding-linux-x64-gnu`, etc.) and do not list `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi`. Consequently, package managers running in WebContainer never install the WASI binding.
   - At runtime, `oxc-parser/src-js/bindings.js` detects WebContainer and falls back to `webcontainer-fallback.cjs`, which attempts to run `childProcess.execFileSync("pnpm", ["i", "@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@..."], { cwd: "/tmp/..." })`.
   - Running this synchronous subprocess from a worker thread inside WebContainer fails (or fails to initialize the multi-threaded WASI runtime), causing the synchronous `require(esm)` evaluation of `oxc-parser` to fail and surface as `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE`.

#### Proposed Solution (Option 4A: Add `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` to `@angular/build` optionalDependencies)

In `oxc-parser/src-js/bindings.js`, before falling back to `webcontainer-fallback.cjs`, it checks:
```js
__napiWasiResolveCandidate('@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi', true, undefined)
```
If `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` is already present in `node_modules`, `oxc-parser` directly loads it and bypasses `webcontainer-fallback.cjs` and the dynamic `pnpm i` in `/tmp` entirely.

A viable solution (Option 4A) is to declare `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` in `@angular/build`'s `optionalDependencies` (similar to how `lmdb` is declared).
This ensures that package managers install the WASI binding up-front alongside `@angular/build`, preventing the runtime dynamic installation and the resulting failure in WebContainer.

### Minimal Reproduction
1. Open https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac?file=package.json (or update any StackBlitz Angular starter to Angular CLI v22.2+).
2. Run `npm install && npm start` (or `ng serve`).
3. Notice the build fails with `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE: Cannot require() ES Module .../oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle`.

### Exception or Error
```
(node:12) ExperimentalWarning: WASI is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
[oxc-parser] Downloading @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.150.0 on WebContainer...
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE]: Cannot require() ES Module /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle. (from /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/@angular/build/src/tools/oxc/oxc-transform.js) A cycle involving require(esm) is not allowed to maintain invariants mandated by the ECMAScript specification. Try making at least part of the dependency in the graph lazily loaded.
    at ModuleLoader.importSyncForRequire (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:169:3960)
    at loadESMFromCJS (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19002)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19068)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:20043)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17661)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:15179)
    at wrapModuleLoad (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:4199)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17842)
    at require2 (node:internal/modules/helpers:177:3126) {
  code: 'ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE'
}

Node.js v22.22.3
```

### Your Environment
```

Node: 22.22.3 (WebContainer)
OS: linux x64 (WebContainer)
```

Issues.Title: Server polyfills are not user-controllable: no way to opt out of `@angular/platform-server/init` or add server-only polyfills
Issues.Body:
### Command

build, serve

### Description

`@angular/build:application` derives the server polyfills list entirely on its own and offers no option to change it. In `createServerPolyfillBundleOptions` ([application-code-bundle.ts#L164-L184](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/application-code-bundle.ts#L164-L184)):

- `zone.js/node` (or `zone.js` on `platform: 'neutral'`) is added when the browser `polyfills` list contains `zone.js`,
- `@angular/localize/init` is added when the browser list contains it,
- `@angular/platform-server/init` is **always** added.

So the browser polyfills list is fully explicit, and the server polyfills list is fully implicit. Two concrete gaps follow from that:

#### 1. There is no opt-out of the `init` global patch

`@angular/platform-server/init` is a side-effectful module whose only job is `Object.assign(globalThis, domino.impl)` plus `globalThis.KeyboardEvent = domino.impl.Event`. The framework introduced it as something an app *may* import before bootstrap for code that touches DOM globals at module-evaluation time ([angular/angular#40559](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/40559)). Most apps do not need it: `platform-server` runs the identical shim itself in `DominoAdapter.makeCurrent()` → `setDomTypes()` on every platform init, so for everything that runs after bootstrap the `init` patch is redundant and is overwritten on the first render anyway.

Since v15 the CLI adds it to every server build with no way to say no. Evidence that people need the opt-out:

- The framework's own SSR benchmarks patch `@angular/build` to strip the `platform-server/init` import from `polyfills.server.mjs` (`modules/ssr-benchmarks/README.md` in angular/angular), and the `main.server.ts` there notes that `ɵENABLE_DOM_EMULATION` "won't prevent the monkey patching of DOM apis as this is introduced by the CLI".
- Anyone running the server bundle outside Node with a real DOM (the benchmark case, or `ENABLE_DOM_EMULATION: false`) gets Domino's classes forced onto `globalThis` regardless.
- Apps that want to keep `globalThis` clean on the server (no `HTMLElement`, `Node`, `Event`, … leaking into third-party code that feature-detects the environment with `typeof window`/`typeof HTMLElement`) have no option either.

Measured on a default `ng new --ssr` app (details in #34514): the `init` module costs ~235 kB on disk, ~1.1 MB of retained heap for the life of the process and ~7 ms of startup, while the `Object.assign` itself is negligible (~7 KB, 0.03 ms). Prerendered and SSR output are byte-identical with and without it.

#### 2. There is nowhere to put a server-only polyfill

The `ssr.platform` option's own description says *"Please note that this feature does not provide polyfills for Node.js modules."* With `platform: 'neutral'` (Cloudflare Workers and similar), users are expected to bring polyfills themselves, yet the only polyfills option feeds the browser bundle. Today a server-only polyfill has to be imported manually at the top of `main.server.ts`, where it runs after `zone.js` and `init` and after any shared chunks.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let `polyfills` take either the current array or a browser/server object, mirroring the existing `outputPath` shape (`string | { base, browser, server, media }`):

```jsonc
"polyfills": ["zone.js"]                                 // today, unchanged
"polyfills": {
  "browser": ["zone.js"],
  "server": ["zone.js/node", "@angular/platform-server/init"]
}
```

Semantics:

- **Array form keeps today's behaviour exactly**: `browser` = the array, `server` = derived as now (`zone.js/node`, localize, `init`). Non-breaking; no migration needed.
- **An explicit `server` list is the server polyfills list**, the same way the browser list already is: the builder adds nothing on top. To drop the `init` global patch, omit it. To keep today's output, list it. The `ng new` / `ssr` schematics can emit the explicit form so new projects see what they get.
- `isZonelessApp` is evaluated per list (browser list for the browser bundle, server list for the server bundle), so `zone.js` vs `zone.js/node` and the async/await support flags fall out naturally.
- `getEsBuildCommonPolyfillsOptions` and the `polyfills.server` bundle are unchanged; only the input list is. Normalization follows the existing `normalizeOptimization` / `normalizeSourceMaps` pattern (a small `normalizePolyfills` in `options.ts`, folding in the string-to-array shim that `browser-esbuild` still relies on).
- Consumers that read `options.polyfills` and would switch to `.browser` / `.server`: `application-code-bundle.ts` (browser bundle, server bundle, `isZonelessApp` checks), `execute-build.ts` (top-level-await hint), `dev-server/vite/index.ts` (`es2016` target), and `browser-esbuild`'s string handling.

This solves both gaps with one option and no new concept: server polyfills become as explicit as browser polyfills.

I am happy to implement this and open the PR once the shape is agreed; the single-copy fix in #34516 is independent of it and already covers the duplicate.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

**A boolean under `ssr`**, next to `ssr.platform`, which already shapes the server polyfill list (`zone.js` vs `zone.js/node`), the `createRequire` banner and the `xhr2` external:

```jsonc
"ssr": { "entry": "src/server.ts", "platform": "node", "domShims": false }
```

One `if` around line 184. It only addresses gap 1, and the name needs care so it is not confused with the framework's private `ɵENABLE_DOM_EMULATION`, which controls the adapter and does not affect the global shims.

**Leaving it manual**: users who want `init` could import it in `main.server.ts` as the v12 schematic did. That would be a breaking change for apps that rely on the implicit import, and it still leaves gap 2.

**Not an alternative, but related**: the same unconditional `init` import is also why the server build currently ships two copies of Domino (#34514). That has a bundling-level fix that does not need this option; this request is about control, not about the duplicate.

### Anything else relevant?

- No spec or e2e currently asserts anything about `polyfills.server.mjs`, `zone.js/node` or `@angular/platform-server/init`; `tests/options/polyfills_spec.ts` only covers `dist/browser/polyfills.js`. Either solution should add a server polyfills spec.
- The webpack server builder only adds `init` when `@angular/platform-server` is installed (`isPackageInstalled` in `webpack/configs/common.ts`); the esbuild path has no equivalent guard.
- Repro and measurements: https://github.com/ChristopherPHolder/ng-double-domino
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Server polyfills are not user-controllable: no way to opt out of `@angular/platform-server/init` or add server-only polyfills" (#34515)

Issues.Title: Feature (MatDialog): Add an option to prevent duplicate dialogs
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

Currently, Angular Material’s MatDialog allows the same component to be opened multiple times, resulting in multiple instances of the same dialog being displayed simultaneously.

In some applications, this behavior is undesirable. For example, repeated user interactions or multiple event emissions can accidentally open the same dialog more than once.

Developers must currently implement their own duplicate detection logic using MatDialog.openDialogs or MatDialog.getDialogById() before calling MatDialog.open().

Proposed solution

It would be useful to have a built-in option in MatDialogConfig to prevent duplicate instances of the same component from being opened.

For example:

this.dialog.open(MyDialogComponent, {
  preventDuplicates: true,
});

When this option is enabled, attempting to open a component that already has an open dialog could either:

* Return the existing MatDialogRef without creating another instance.
* Ignore the new request and keep the existing dialog open.

The exact behavior could be determined by the maintainers.

Ideally, duplicate detection would be scoped to the component type, with an option to customize the behavior if needed.

Benefits

* Avoids accidentally opening multiple instances of the same dialog.
* Reduces repetitive boilerplate across applications.
* Provides a consistent, framework-level solution.
* Keeps applications simpler and less error-prone.

Alternatives considered

Currently, developers can manually inspect openDialogs or use getDialogById() before opening a dialog. However, this requires additional application-level logic and does not provide a straightforward, reusable option for this common use case.

Would this feature be a good fit for Angular Material’s MatDialog API? I’d be happy to contribute a PR if the maintainers consider this approach appropriate.

### Use Case

_No response_

Issues.Title: bug(aria/accordion): Enter/Space inside a panel toggles the accordion instead of activating the focused element
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Enter on a link (or Space on a button) inside an expanded `ngAccordionPanel` collapses the panel instead of activating the link/button.

`ngAccordionGroup` handles `keydown` for the whole group, including panel content, and calls `preventDefault()` on Enter/Space, so the focused element never gets activated. Arrow keys and Home/End are affected too, e.g. Home in an input inside a panel moves focus to the trigger.

The click handler only reacts to events coming from a trigger (`_findTriggerPattern`), the keydown handler doesn't check that:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/952685f9370ba718f832d745512db7c9a04e1bcd/src/aria/private/accordion/accordion.ts#L73-L97

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/z5sxyaq6?file=src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Expand "Section 1".
2. Tab to "Link inside panel" or "Button inside panel" and press Enter / Space.
3. Expand it again, click into the input and press Home.

### Expected Behavior

The link/button is activated (shows up in the log) and the panel stays open. Home moves the caret in the input.

### Actual Behavior

The panel collapses, nothing is activated. Home moves focus to the trigger.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: @angular/aria 22.2.4 (also 22.1.6)
- Browser(s): Chrome 155
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Linux
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "bug(aria/accordion): Enter/Space inside a panel toggles the accordion instead of activating the focused element" (#34011)

Issues.Title: build: guard branch-manager against forks and harden checkout
Issues.Body:
This change restores `if: github.event.repository.fork == false` on `.github/workflows/assistant-to-the-branch-manager.yml` on the `22.2.x` branch per GHSS `pull_request_target` policy remediation (b/577107676).

Because 100% of pull requests in `angular/components` originate from forks (`only_allow_releasable_branches: true`) and `branch-manager` requires `context.eventName === 'pull_request_target'` along with `secrets.ANGULAR_ROBOT_PRIVATE_KEY` to set mergeability commit status, the previous `head.repo.fork == false` check caused all fork PR runs to be skipped. Restoring the base repository fork check ensures branch-manager triggers as intended on upstream PRs while preventing runs on external forks.

Additionally, `persist-credentials: false` is added to `actions/checkout` in `.github/workflows/google-internal-tests.yml` for defense-in-depth.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "build: guard branch-manager against forks and harden checkout" (#34007)

Issues.Title: bug(ClickEventManager): Clicks on iOS 18.2 and before do not have pointer type
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

I found this problem using the listbox component, but I am pretty sure all components that use the ClickEventManager have this problem. iOS versions older than 18.2 do not have a pointer type, the ClickEventManager sees these as fake clicks (see isFakeClick function) and ignores them, so clicks do not work.

See release notes about the pointer type.
https://webkit.org/blog/16301/webkit-features-in-safari-18-2/

### Reproduction

Can be reproduced on https://angular.dev with a iOS version older than 18.2, with multiple components for example on https://angular.dev/guide/aria/select.

### Expected Behavior

Clicks in components handeld via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 should work.

### Actual Behavior

Clicks in components handled via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 do not work.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: 22.2.3
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): iOS version older than 18.2
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "bug(ClickEventManager): Clicks on iOS 18.2 and before do not have pointer type" (#33999)

Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "build: update dependency node to v22.23.4 (main)" (#34002)

Issues.Title: refactor(cdk/testing): remove msMatchesSelector fallback
Issues.Body: Removes the fallback to the IE-only `msMatchesSelector` in the TestBed and Selenium WebDriver test elements, since `Element.matches` is supported in every browser we support. The deprecated Protractor test element is left unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(cdk/testing): remove msMatchesSelector fallback" (#34001)

Issues.Title: refactor(material/core): remove unused private theming variables
Issues.Body: Removes private Sass variables in the theming files that aren't referenced anywhere. The compiled CSS of the prebuilt themes and the theming tests is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(material/core): remove unused private theming variables" (#34000)

Issues.Title: fix(multiple): avoid duplicate required error with signal forms
Issues.Body:
When a checkbox or slide toggle is bound to a signal forms field whose schema uses `required()`, signal forms set the component's `required` input and also run the component's own validator. This resulted in two `required` errors, and the one from the component doesn't have the message from the schema, which hides it when using `getError('required')`.

These changes skip the component's `required` validation when it's bound to a signal forms field, since the schema already handles it.

Fixes #33945.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(multiple): avoid duplicate required error with signal forms" (#33990)

Issues.Title: fix(material/menu): do not pull focus out of an overlay opened by a menu item
Issues.Body:
When a menu item opens an overlay, like a dialog, that focuses its content before the menu closes (e.g. when animations are disabled), the menu would restore focus to its trigger behind the overlay. These changes skip restoring focus when the menu is closed by a click and focus has moved into a different overlay. Focus is still restored if it's in another menu (e.g. when clicking an item in a sub-menu), in the overlay containing the trigger, or outside of any overlay.

Fixes #33967.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/menu): do not pull focus out of an overlay opened by a menu item" (#33989)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): avoid re-rendering when unrelated elements are added
Issues.Body:
Updates the `SortedCollection` so it doesn't emit changes when a DOM node that's not a member of the collection is added. I also did some internal cleanup so we don't need to re-create the `Set` all the time and to keep a version counter.

Fixes #33976.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(aria/menu): avoid re-rendering when unrelated elements are added" (#33996)

Issues.Title: fix(material/checkbox): duplicate required error with signal forms
Issues.Body:
The checkbox has a custom required error in template/reactive forms. When it's used together with the signal forms interop, it was causing double `required` errors to show up. These changes skip the custom validation when signal forms are present.

Also fixes a similar issue with the slide toggle.

Fixes #33945.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/checkbox): duplicate required error with signal forms" (#33998)

Issues.Title: docs(cdk/scrolling): explain how to react to scroll events
Issues.Body:
Adds a section to the scrolling overview that shows how to listen to scroll events with `cdkScrollable` and the `ScrollDispatcher`, along with a live example.

Fixes #9594 
The scrolling overview only had two short paragraphs about `cdkScrollable` and `ScrollDispatcher` and didn't show how to actually listen to scroll events. This adds:

- a section on `elementScrolled`, `scrolled` and `ancestorScrolled`, with a snippet
- a live example (`cdk-scrollable-overview`) that shows the scroll offset and scrolls back to the top
- a note that the events fire outside the Angular zone, so the view only updates if you use signals or `markForCheck`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs(cdk/scrolling): explain how to react to scroll events" (#33997)
